# Traders Adda project memory

## CURRENT RULES (read this first; where an older section below disagrees, this block wins)

- **The tested strategy** ("Blue sky + Multi-year breakouts"): buy a breakout on the Blue sky or Multi-year breakouts screen on the day it breaks out (next open); stop **12%** below the buy (8% is the "tighter option"); risk 2% of the account with a 20% position cap, so a 12% stop means a smaller position; exit when the stock closes under its 50-day average; at most 10 positions and 3 new buys a day; 0.25% cost a side. Source of the numbers: `scripts/backtest-winrate.mjs`, `backtest-variants.mjs`, `backtest-recent.mjs`.
- **The market check (`src/lib/screen/setupGate.ts`)**: real buys only while at least **35%** of liquid stocks are above their 50-day average. The Nifty 50 against its 200-day average is information only, NOT a rule (it was fragile in the tests). Top picks, the checklist, the trade plan, the Today strip and both emails use this one check.
- **Targets** are only places to book part profit: +16% and +24% price levels. Fixed targets lost most of the profit in the tests.
- **The paper test**: the Live strategy check (`/tracker`, `.cache/strategy-tracker.json`) runs these exact rules, started 31 Oct 2026 with a 12% stop, no Nifty filter, 10 lakh paper money. Judge it after 30 closed trades; the strategy health monitor warns if the edge fades.
- **Real trades** are recorded on `/positions` (`.cache/positions.json`, daily backups in `.cache/backups`, CSV download). The app never places orders; automated trading was deliberately not built.
- **Older scanner sections** (Buy ready, watch list, bullish confluence, bottomed-out, 52-week-high) are a separate, older rule set with their own stops and a stricter 50% breadth gate; their own backtest shows no proven edge. A stock that is in Top picks shows "Trade plan: see Top picks above" there instead of a second plan.
- **Honest caveats**: the 10-year history only contains stocks listed today (no delisted companies), so the backtest is optimistic; treat the quoted ~46% a year as a ceiling. Rejected after testing (do not retry without new evidence): minimum RS 90/93, breadth gate 45%, ATR stops, fixed targets, faster exits, break-even stops, confirmation entries, time stops, drawdown brake, add-to-winners.
- **Never reuse** `/api/health` (the start-up check used by `scripts/start-local-app.ps1`); the strategy health feature is `/api/strategy-health`.

## Product direction

- Horizon plans are shown as REFERENCE LEVELS (4 Oct 2026, user decision, reversing the same day's hide): the research table (`BuyIdeaTable`), drawer (`ReferenceLevels`) and watchlist show entry/SL/T1/T2 with the historical hit rates from `src/lib/screen/horizonBacktest.json` (`horizonTargetOdds` in `horizonOdds.ts`, Buy ready sample; `targetOddsLines`; `MIN_ODDS_TRADES` = 100 flags small samples) plus `HORIZON_RESEARCH_NOTE` ('Reference levels, not a recommendation'). Regenerate with `node --no-warnings scripts/backtest-horizons.mjs --write`. Never present them as recommendations or claim an edge: short −0.16R (T1 17%), mid +0.02R (T1 33%), long +0.32R on 32 trades. Today's Picks stays the tested buy list and must stay unchanged. The drawer does not log journal trades. Plan rules:  short = `tradeLevels` (10-day swing low, 1–2.5 ATR, 2R/3R). Mid and long stops sit below real swing lows from `TradeLevels.swingLow20`/`swingLow50` (`SWING_STOP_RULES` in `horizonSignal.ts`: mid 20-day low − 0.25 ATR, min 1.5 ATR, risk ≤ 8%, 2R/3R; long 50-day low − 0.5 ATR, min 2 ATR, risk ≤ 10%, 2.5R/4R). Never cap the stop at the max risk percentage — wide support must fail the risk check. Price at/through the swing stop means no plan. Every horizon has a "Price above stop-loss" check. `plan.stopBasis` explains the stop in the stock drawer. When the risk or stop check fails, `finishSignal` sets `plan = null` and `noTrade` ("Risk too wide – no trade" / "Below stop-loss – no trade", user decision 4 Oct 2026, after CUPID showed a +35% short-term T2); never display targets for such stocks. `nearestBuyIdeas` keeps them with the reason. Holding labels come from `HORIZON_HOLDING` (short up to 30 trading days, mid ~3 months, long 6–12 months). Tests: `scripts/horizon-signal.test.mjs`.

- Snapshot data quality (4 Oct 2026, user-approved): `historyQuality.ts` validates every equity/benchmark history in the universe sweep. Structural faults (non-numeric, negative volume, future, duplicate/unordered sessions) exclude the symbol; impossible OHLC keeps only sessions after the latest invalid bar (user chose this over excluding) and is reported. Expired cached history after a failed refresh is used only when consensus of fresh histories confirms no missing session before the quote session; unverifiable continuity excludes. `mergeQuoteIntoCandles` never shrinks a same-session high/low/volume and ignores quotes >5 min in the future. Quotes without provider timestamps are dropped (never stamped "now"); Kite zone-less times are IST (`kiteTime.ts`). Yahoo chart parsing lives in `yahooChart.ts` (null closes skipped without shifting timestamps). Snapshot `dataQuality` and ready-state `refreshFailure` flow through screen/scanner/monthly APIs to `DataQualityNotice`. Do not loosen these checks to regain coverage. Tests: `scripts/history-quality.test.mjs`, `scripts/candle-merge.test.mjs`.

- Stock research breadth comparison (3 Oct 2026): off-by-default, nonpersisted checkbox affects only research long ideas and near misses by simulating a passing breadth value. Show measured breadth and normal versus hypothetical counts with selected universe/horizon; label simulated badges/plans non-actionable. Never apply it to dashboard metrics, drawers, shorts, monthly setups, Picks, emails or paper approvals. Keep all stock checks, risk flags and liquidity unchanged. Reload restores normal mode; tests in `scripts/command-center.test.mjs`.

- Monthly Setups (3 Oct 2026): user approved latest completed-month close strictly above prior 12 completed monthly highs, plus most-recent mother candle with >=2 subsequent fully contained completed months through latest month (equality inside allowed). Separate `#monthly-setups` Scanner tools workspace/API; do not add home panels or email sources. Reuse snapshot, placeholder filtering and liquidity floor. Reject malformed/stale or nonconsecutive monthly history; discard initial partial month, check first/last scheduled boundaries, require >=13 complete months. Calendar completion uses final scheduled session close and ignores force-live simulation. Monthly Wilder DMI/ADX(14), RS, volume ratio and range-height projections are research context, not gates or probabilities. Current-month observations never confirm signals. Existing Short status is displayed only with aligned scan provenance. Keep unavailable indicators/history and provider failures explicit. No proprietary MB/Fisher/Ichimoku port or proven-profit claims. Tests: `scripts/monthly-setups.test.mjs`.

- Summary-only dashboard (3 Oct 2026, supersedes inline metric lists and hidden home research): `CommandCenter` has today/metrics/research/directory views. Home mounts no metric table, confluence panels or scanner directory and does not poll scanner/RSI feeds. Click cards to dedicated `#metric-*` workspaces with Back action and selector; full membership semantics stay unchanged. Stock research and Scanner directory have dedicated hashes/menu/quick actions. Compact pulse moves explanatory text into its disclosure; morning brief stays collapsed. Horizon is lifted to Dashboard to preserve it across in-app views; shared metric URLs use default Short horizon. Preserve data failures, breadth/filter scope and research-vs-Picks distinction.

- Dashboard redesign (3 Oct 2026): focused home keeps index snapshot, pulse, breadth/research metrics and next-step links visible; morning/global brief, stock research/session changes and scanner directory use native disclosures. Do not remove their content or treat research counts as curated Today's Picks. Sidebar shows Dashboard, Picks, Market overview, Watchlist, Paper trades & journal, grouped Scanner tools and About & risk. Market children stay in page tabs; Trade Triggers uses `SCANNER_NAV_GROUPS` in a grouped select with counts, not a long sidebar submenu. Existing hashes, Back/Forward, stock drawers, filtering, theme and all trading/email rules remain unchanged. Sidebar is 232px / 72px collapsed, with a 64px icon rail below lg; narrow header moves search to its own row. This supersedes older always-expanded menu/panel and header sizing descriptions below.

- Index emails (3 Oct 2026, current decision supersedes the older hourly skip-on-no-changes policy): shared `alerts/indexEmailFormat.ts` renders completed pre-open Nifty/Bank/IT/Midcap context and provisional hourly index snapshots in HTML/plain text. `hourlyEmailPreview` is async; await every consumer. Every real hourly NSE slot sends even with unchanged stock membership; stock sections show full lists with a Status column (5 Oct 2026). `emailSlotKey` rejects actual holidays/weekends, off-hours and `MARKET_FORCE_LIVE`. Preserve `EMAIL_AUTO_SEND` gating. Current index quotes come from the selected provider, are merged into live daily histories only when recent, and carry unverified-latency warnings. Compare prices against `lastIndexes` from the last successful email (same provider/day, increasing timestamp, quotes within 5 minutes); never call this exactly-one-hour return or hourly candles. Breadth deltas require <=90 s snapshot age, same date/membership and full coverage. Compare price with genuine saved pre-open levels; explicitly label previous-close references if no morning record exists. Flag resistance-break/weak-breadth conflicts without creating trade gates. Keep delayed/missing data visible; never imply exchange-verified real time, sustained intraday confirmation, VWAP or OI. Previews and failed sends do not advance baselines; state read failures must not silently discard baselines. Hourly (live) index layout (5 Oct 2026, user asked for clear/crisp/short): `liveIndexSection` renders one blue takeaway sentence (Nifty move + morning-range position, other indexes that broke S/R, Nifty breadth weak/mixed/strong, conflict caution), one 4-column table (Index + price + day range | Today % with "since last" | R/S whole numbers | Read: verdict pill Inside range / Above resistance / Below support / Levels n/a / "Above R · weak breadth", breadth % above 50 DMA with 5d and since-last pp, Daily/Week trend, amber ⚠ flags for delayed quote, no saved plan (previous-close levels), prior-session breadth, stale/missing history), one shortened Leadership + VIX line and a single muted footnote with the latency / not-OI / forming-candle caveats. Pre-open (completed) index layout unchanged.

- Index outlook journal: `indexOutlookJournal.ts` freezes the first real, fresh completed pre-open reading during trading-day 08:45-09:15 IST, never backfills and rejects mock/simulated captures. `indexContext.ts` supplies actual daily index histories; the no-browser `autoRefresh.ts` timer invokes it in capture/post-close windows. Evaluate only exact target-date completed OHLC after close, freeze evaluations, report touches/crossings/closing side and ambiguous order when both sides cross; no fills, returns or win-rate claims. `.cache/index-outlook-journal.json` persists up to 1,000 captured trading dates using serialized atomic writes for one server process. Preserve it when clearing market caches. API/UI expose an honest empty state and storage errors; multiple instances need shared storage/locking.

- Index analysis: `indexAnalysis.ts` reuses Wilder RSI and `wilderAtr` from `oscillators.ts`; preserves the original 20-session range and adds nearby completed-day/week, confirmed 2+2 swing and MA references. Daily trend = close/20/50 alignment + 50 slope; weekly = completed weeks only, 10/30 alignment + 30 slope (configured holidays respected). Shared `indexContext.ts` supplies `/api/market/index-analysis?mode=completed|live` and pre-open Nifty/Bank outlook. Index page defaults to completed, quotes/chart remain independent, live daily is explicitly provisional. Verified Nifty50/Bank/IT/Midcap100 memberships are stored in `index-analysis-membership.json`, imported together from official CSVs by `npm run update-index-membership` with count/duplicate validation. `indexParticipation.ts` uses exact-session histories, window-specific denominators, and a common cohort (at least 80% coverage) for five-index-session change in above-50-DMA percentage points. This uses current, not point-in-time membership; never substitute broad-market breadth. `indexLevelRanking.ts` clusters within 0.15 ATR (0.1% without ATR), prevents chained merges, deduplicates reference labels, and scores swing=4, weekly/200DMA=3, 50DMA=2, other=1 (Major >=4, Intermediate >=2); significance is not win probability. `indexDataQuality.ts` rejects malformed/future/duplicate sessions and distinguishes expected live vs completed sessions, including pre-open/holidays. Exact Midcap Yahoo history currently has one daily bar: no technical analysis or five-session trend, no ETF substitution, but session-aligned constituent participation may still appear. Leadership is fresh, aligned 20-session relative return in percentage points, not weighted contribution; VIX is risk context, not directional certainty. UI/email share these outputs. Scenarios are conditional and do not alter recommendation/trading gates.

- Local unattended startup: `scripts/install-local-startup.ps1` registers the visible, current-user Windows task "Traders Adda Local Startup" (08:45 IST weekdays + login, interactive/limited privileges, retries failures, no wake/sleep changes). `scripts/start-local-app.ps1` runs the existing production build on loopback port 3107, holds a named mutex to avoid duplicate launchers, verifies an existing listener via `/api/health`, and writes process logs to `.cache/startup/`. Never bypass organization execution policies or expose this listener publicly. `src/lib/market/autoRefresh.ts`, started by instrumentation, warms/refreshes the shared universe with no browser required; it preserves snapshot TTLs (1 minute live, 15 minutes closed), prevents overlapping ticks, and logs refresh errors. This does not automate the browser-local paper engine.

- This is a desktop-first NSE technical-analysis web workstation, not a mobile application.
- Keep one consistent workspace design: dark slate gradient hero, uppercase green eyebrow, large title, concise description, optional actions, tab cards where appropriate, compact filter toolbar, sticky table headers/identity columns, internal table scrolling, and no page-level horizontal overflow.
- Reuse `src/components/WorkspaceShell.tsx` instead of creating another page-specific header or outer card style.
- A scanner discovers candidates; it is not a recommendation. Act only on Buy ready status (see "Unified status and Today's Picks"), adequate liquidity, aligned trend, supportive breadth, and a valid entry/stop/target plan before presenting an actionable bullish idea.
- Ratings represent the percentage of required technical checks passing, not win probability.

## Main workspace structure

- `Monthly Setups`: completed monthly breakout/compression research, fetched only while this view is open. Listed in shared scanner directory with counts explicitly available only in its own workspace. `monthlyCalendar.ts` pins annual NSE regular-session holidays from CMTR59722/FAOP65588/CMTR71775 (2024–2026) plus environment closures for monthly boundaries only; do not alter other calendars incidentally. Retain real special-session bars in aggregation. A merged final-day quote from before its close cannot confirm monthly OHLC. Shared ADX helper requires >=29 monthly bars.

- `Core Setups`: VCP is the primary swing setup. Blue Sky is confirmation, Multi-year Breakouts is for position trading, and IPO Base is a special situation.
- `RPCI & Oscillators`: contraction discovery and momentum timing live together inside one shared workspace shell.
- `RSI Edge Scanners`: Daily Bullish, Weekly Bullish, and Bearish.
- `Trade Triggers`: grouped Scanner Pro-style — MVP picks (Fresh 52W High, Trend Pullback, Relative Leader), Breakout (Range Breakout, NR7, All-Time High), Pro strategies (Pocket Pivot), Reversal (Four-Day Fall & Reversal), Experimental (RSI Divergence).
- `Watchlist`: fixed Nifty 50 coverage plus optional personal symbols, independent Buy and Short ratings, horizon-specific plans, and modern sticky table.
- `Market`: isolated workspace with All Breakouts, Breadth, Rotation, Sector Strength, and Map tabs.
- `About & Risk`: isolated guidance workspace; do not make it a footer-only navigation target.

## Scanner curation

- Normal navigation intentionally hides Swing Trading SPECIAL, Up 3% × 3 Days, Close Above 21 EMA, and Inside Bar.
- Do not re-add those scanners to the primary navigation without explicit user approval:
  - Swing Trading SPECIAL is incomplete until quarterly EPS, ROCE, and ROE are available.
  - Inside Bar uses a non-textbook and excessively broad published definition.
  - Up 3% × 3 Days commonly identifies already-extended moves.
  - A fresh 21 EMA cross is a confirmation signal, not a standalone trade setup.
- `SCANNER_NAV_GROUPS` controls visible Trade Trigger navigation.
- `ALERT_SCANNER_KEYS` controls recommendation-email scanner sources and is intentionally limited to Range Breakout, NR7, and Four-Day Fall & Reversal.
- The underlying scanner calculations may remain for compatibility and analysis even when hidden from normal navigation.

## Scanner Pro Phase 1 (scanner.mrchartist.com, 1 October 2026)

- Source: Scanner Pro's public catalogue and `scoreMeta` bundle; the real app is behind Google login — never sign in with the user's account. Intraday, F&O/OI and order-flow scans cannot be built (no intraday or OI data).
- Five daily scans added (user-approved for navigation; `chartinkSlug: null`, notes say "Scanner Pro-style; formula is ours"; rules in `MVP_SCAN_RULES`):
  - `high52`: close > prior 252-session high and volume ≥ 1.5× 50-day average.
  - `pullback20`: close > SMA50 > SMA200, SMA200 rising 20d, EMA20 rising 5d, low ≤ EMA20 × 1.015, close ≥ EMA20, a close ≥ 3% above EMA20 in the prior 10 sessions. Buy ready plan: entry = day high, stop basis = day low.
  - `leader`: RS line (close ÷ NIFTY50) above its prior 252-session max (≥ 200 aligned days), RS rating ≥ 90 (stands in for Scanner Pro's sector top-3 — most stocks lack a sector), close > SMA50.
  - `ath`: close above all held history (≥ 500 sessions; we hold ~3 years, so it is a 3-year high and is labelled so), RSI 60–75.
  - `pocket`: up day, volume > largest down-day volume of prior 10 sessions, close within SMA10…SMA10 × 1.05, close > SMA50 > SMA200.
- The universe snapshot now carries `benchmark` (NIFTY50 history, cached at `.cache/daily-candles/yahoo/NIFTY50.json`); `benchmarkCloses()` maps it by IST day for `runScanners(…, {marketCapCr, rs, benchmark})`.
- Backtest (T1/T2, 0.25% cost, 2022-10 → 2026-09), Buy ready: leader +0.42R (27 trades, best), ath +0.13R (31), pocket 0.00R (234), pullback20 −0.05R (1,216), high52 −0.21R (45). `ALERT_SCANNER_KEYS` stays range/nr7/fall4; leader/ath are candidates once samples grow. The backtest ANY row counts alert keys only (−0.03R, 260 trades) and feeds the email footer.
- Price Action Rating (`priceActionRating.ts`, 0–100; Trend 20, Momentum 20, Leadership 15, Volume 5, Stability 40; deductions gap-fade −6, climax −8, thin ₹1–5 Cr up to −12; Illiquid < ₹1 Cr; Not rated < 200 sessions). Raw points are calibrated by `priceActionCalibration.ts` (generated by `scripts/backtest-rating.mjs --write`: p25→35, p50→50, p80→70, p95→85). Grades D/C/B/A/A+ at 35/50/70/85.
- Rating study (80k ratings): A+ beats the day's median by +2.2% over 20 sessions and +5.1% over 60, best grade in both halves; D oddly beats C. But PA grade does **not** improve scanner stop-buy R-trades, so it is a display/research score only — RS ranking stays for emails. Shown as a column/sort on Trade Triggers and a card in the drawer.

## RSI Edge source integrity

- Chartink hides the clauses for the three RSI Edge scanners. Never claim to reproduce their hidden logic and never infer membership from locally guessed conditions.
- Scanner membership must come from the public Chartink result response through `src/lib/screen/rsiEdgeChartink.ts` and `/api/market/rsi-edge`.
- Local RSI, pivot, Buy, and Short calculations are supplemental columns only; they must never add or remove a stock from an RSI Edge result set.
- Fetch the three source scanners independently. A failure in one tab must not hide successful results from the other tabs.
- Never display partial membership for a failed scanner. Retained data after a failed refresh must be marked stale.
- Chartink counts can change during market hours because its public scan uses delayed market data.

## Alerts

- Telegram is unsupported in this environment.
- Do not expose Telegram controls, start its scheduler, or restore Telegram environment variables.
- `/api/alerts/telegram` intentionally returns HTTP 410 for GET and POST.
- Hourly email remains supported. Recommendation attachments must contain only Buy ready ideas and use the curated scanner sources.

### Recommendation quality (decided 30 September 2026)

- Customer emails (`buildAlertTable(..., { recommendationsOnly: true })`) carry **Buy ready only** as calls: every check passes, market breadth included. On a weak-breadth day there are no calls and the email says "not buying is the plan". Do not pad the call list.
- The same table also carries `watch` = "Strong stocks waiting for the market" (Today's Picks watch list). It is built from **all** `SCANNER_KEYS` rows with Watch status that pass `WATCH_RULES` (`passesWatchRules`: turnover ≥ ₹40 Cr, PA rating ≥ 76, RS ≥ 75, stop ≤ 6%), ranked by RS, max 2 per sector (`capPerSector`), **no count cap** in `todaysPicks().watch` (user decision 4 Oct 2026: the Today's Picks page shows every qualifying stock; the emails trim to 5 themselves via `.slice(0, 5)` in `hourlyEmail.ts`/`hourlyEmailFormat.ts`/`preOpenEmailFormat.ts`); RPCI/Oscillator extras no longer feed it. `scripts/backtest-weak-watch.mjs` showed buying these on weak-breadth days loses (−0.14R quality top 5; −0.06R all scanners), so it is **labelled "do not buy"**: both emails render it via the shared `src/lib/alerts/watchEmail.ts` (`watchHtml`/`watchText`) in a compact layout: an orange "DO NOT BUY YET" line with `watchReason`, then **one table** (Stock + main screener + "Also in: …" + RS | Trigger with close | Stop loss with % | Target 1 with T2 under it), optional **Added / Unchanged / Removed** tags, and a one-line filters footnote (RS 75+ · Chart grade A · Turnover ₹40 Cr+ · SL within 6% · Max 2 per sector). The pre-open passes no previous list, so it shows no tags. Prices are rounded (whole ₹ from ₹1,000, else 1 decimal). **Branding:** both emails use `brandHeader`/`brandFooter` from `src/lib/alerts/brand.ts` (colours from the user's logo: canvas `#020814`, panel `#0b1526`, green `#22c55e`). Design system in `brand.ts`: `BRAND_STYLE` (mobile rules: `.pad`, `.outer`, `.col`, `.logo`, `.lv`), `brandHeader` (4px green top bar, dark canvas, kicker/title/subtitle on the **left** and the logo **top-right** at 130px, then stat tiles), `brandSection(icon, title, {note, right})` (navy badge with green number/icon), `rulesCard` (numbered swing rules) and `brandFooter`. Pre-open layout (compact, user asked for 'short and crisp, one table per section'): tiles Bias / Breadth / Buy ready (or Watching), a one-line green 'Levels and ideas are final' + regime strip, 1 Opening bias as one tinted strip (big signed %, label, top-4 driver chips from `bias.components`; grey when |bias| < 0.15%), 2 Global cues as **one 4-column table** (Market | Chg | Market | Chg, every cue line flattened), 3 Key levels as **one table** (Index + close/chg | dark 'Likely range' pill | Pivot with S1·R1), then Buy ready, watch and 52W sections as compact tables from `src/lib/alerts/compactEmail.ts` (`dataTable` with class `dt`, `TRADE_COLUMNS` = Stock · screener | Buy above/Trigger | Stop loss | Target (T2 under T1), `stockCell` with screener + 'Also in', `levelCells`, `tag`). Methodology text sits in one footnote. Verified no horizontal scroll at 360px (BRAND_STYLE `.dt td` trims padding on phones). **Hourly = changes only** (user decision 2026-10-03): `hourlyChanges`/`buildHourlyEmail(table, now, baseline)` compare against the last hourly email of the day (`lastBuy`/`lastWatch`/`lastDay` in `.cache/email-alert.json`) or, for the day's first slot, the pre-open list (completed-mode table). It shows New Buy ready this hour (table + rules), 'No longer Buy ready' and 'Still Buy ready' as one-line name lists, watch additions (Added) and drops (Removed) via `watchHtml(added, table, dropped)`, and 'Unchanged on watch' as one line. A stock moving watch → Buy ready counts as a new buy, not a drop. When nothing changed the scheduler **skips the send** (records `lastSkippedSlotKey`); manual POST /api/alerts/email forces a send. The hourly no longer attaches the Buy-ready PNG. The footer is dark with the tagline "TRADE | LEARN | ANALYSE | GROW TOGETHER", the 1% risk line and disclaimers. The logo is `public/brand/traders-adda-logo-email.jpg` (440×304, cropped from `traders-adda-logo-original.jpg`, edges feathered into `#020814` so no box shows). It is attached inline as `cid:traders-adda-logo` by `logoAttachment()` in `brandAssets.ts` for both senders. Browser previews (`GET /api/alerts/email?html=1`, `GET /api/alerts/preopen?html=1`) swap the CID for the public path via `withPreviewLogo`. Never present it as trades unless a new backtest shows an edge. Both emails label every stock a **Swing trade** (days to weeks, max 30 sessions; never intraday or long-term) and, only when there are Buy-ready rows, add a "How to trade these swing setups" box from `src/lib/alerts/swingTrade.ts` (`SWING_RULES` mirrors the backtest: 3-day entry window, skip price, 1% risk sizing, half at T1 + stop to cost, T2, 30-session time exit); that box replaces the "Buy only above the trigger" footer line. Top long/short ideas are **not** emailed: the short-term ones duplicate this watch list and the mid/long horizons have no positive backtest. (The hourly "changes only" layout above was replaced on 5 Oct 2026 by full lists with a Status column and a not-a-buy Bullish confluence section; see the Confluence notes.)
- RPCI and Oscillator picks used to take their status from breadth alone and skipped the quality gate (that is how 10%-stop, low-RS names reached customers). `extraSections()` now computes `ExtraPick.failed` through `extraPickFailures` (RS ≥ 70, above the 50- and 200-day averages, ≤ 8% over the 21 EMA, SL ≤ 6%; liquidity is already required to get in). Gated picks rank first; a failing pick shows as "Watch only" with its failures and never appears in recommendations. A pick without `failed` (old cache) counts as unchecked.
- **Backtest honesty:** the footer (`backtestSentence`) reports `ANY.ready.targets`, the T1/T2 exits the alert tells people to use, plus the recent half and the cost. It adds "No proven edge yet" while avg R < `PROVEN_EDGE_R` (0.1). Never quote the `highwin` 80% win rate to customers: it carries 0.00R average gain. The RPCI and Oscillator extras have no backtest.

### Ranking and shorts (backtest study, 30 September 2026)

- **Rank long ideas by RS.** Studies used the `backtest-scanners.mjs` harness with the T1/T2 exit and 0.25% cost, over Oct 2022 to Sep 2026. RS was the only score that improved results steadily: RS < 50 at −0.19R, 70–79 at −0.08R, 80–89 at −0.06R, 90+ at −0.02R (+0.08R since Oct 2025).
  - The oscillator score did not help. Among stocks passing everything but breadth, Osc 10+ was the worst bucket (−0.15R).
  - `alertPicks`, `topScannerPick` (inside a tier), the `recommendationsOnly` rows (re-numbered) and `rankBuyIdeas` (inside a status) all sort by RS.
- **GainzAlgo "Adaptive Regression Breakout Map" is not adopted (2 Oct 2026).**
  - `scripts/backtest-arbm.mjs` copies its open-source Pine logic, long side only. The setup is a 50-bar linear regression ± 2 standard deviations. A squeeze means bandwidth in the bottom 20% of its 100-bar range, and the signal is a close crossing above the upper band right after a squeeze. Stop is the previous lower band; TP1/2/3 are 1/2/3× bandwidth, with the stop trailed to entry and then to TP1.
  - Every variant loses: −0.09R as published, −0.05R even with breadth ≥ 50%.
  - The median stop is about 16% from entry, so a 3–5% stop or a 1% risk rule cannot be used with it.
  - Its dashboard counts TP1-then-breakeven as a win, which shows about 48% against a real win rate of about 27%. Its trendlines are drawn on the chart only and never trigger trades.
  - GainzAlgo V2 Alpha itself sits inside the invite-only, closed-source "GainzAlgo Suite" and cannot be tested.
  - At the user's request (2 Oct 2026) it is available as a tool, not a recommendation: `src/lib/chart/regressionBreakout.ts` ports the Pine script bar by bar (`regressionBreakoutMap`, quirks kept: managed on the signal bar, TP3 before stop, indicator win rate counts TP1-then-breakeven). ProChart overlay "Regression Breakout" (off by default) draws the channel (grey = squeeze), Long/Short markers, entry/stop/TP1–3 map, pivot trendlines and a 4-card panel showing the indicator's own stats next to the real win rate and avg R. The Trade Trigger scan `arbm` (Experimental, long only, `arbmLongSignal`) lists today's signals with band stop and TP columns; its Buy-ready plan uses our swing stop, not the band. It is not in `ALERT_SCANNER_KEYS` or any email. Tests: `scripts/regression-breakout.test.mjs`.
- **Server-side paper trading engine (14 Oct 2026).** The paper portfolio moved from browser localStorage to `.cache/paper-portfolio.json`; `src/lib/paper/paperServer.ts` runs a background loop (started in `instrumentation.ts`, every 5 s while the market is live, 60 s otherwise) that advances pending and open orders with `advancePaperOrder` against provider quotes, so entries, stops and targets work with the page closed. Rules in `paperRules.ts` (tests `scripts/paper-rules.test.mjs`): max 8 pending+open orders, daily loss limit 2% and weekly 5% of starting capital (a hit stops new entries and approvals; open positions keep their stops), estimated delivery charges and 0.05% slippage per fill for net P&L, and stats (win rate, expectancy in R, profit factor, drawdown). Telegram alerts for fills, stops, expiries and a 15:40 IST day summary (`PAPER_TELEGRAM=0` turns them off). API: `GET/POST /api/paper` (actions approve, cancel, close, capital, settings, removeDemo, import). The hook `usePaperTrading` polls it; a browser portfolio is imported once and kept as `sa.paperTrading.v1.migrated`. Limits: fills use the last sampled price (about every 5 s), not tick high/low; charges are estimates.
- **Fyers morning login reminder (14 Oct 2026).** `src/lib/fyers/fyersReminder.ts` (rules in `reminderRules.ts`): on trading days, if today's Fyers login is missing it sends Telegram reminders at 08:45, 09:00 and 09:10 (none after 09:25) and a confirmation once connected. `FYERS_AUTO_OPEN_LOGIN=1` also opens the login page in this PC's default browser at the first reminder (Windows only). The login itself needs your password and one-time code each day; it is not automated.
- **Index Paper Desk (14 Oct 2026).** `/scalp/index-paper`: Nifty and Bank Nifty near-month FUTURES, long or short, in lots, paper only. Pure rules in `src/lib/paper/indexPaper.ts` (tests `scripts/index-paper.test.mjs`): market or breakout-trigger orders, stop, optional target, 15:15 intraday square-off or carry, fills at the observed price (a gap through a stop fills at the next price), Scalp Desk futures costs, 12% margin estimate, 1% risk per order, max 3 trades and 2 losers a day, 2% day and 5% week loss limits. `indexPaperServer.ts` stores `.cache/paper-index.json`, resolves the front contract (the month with more volume), and a 4-second loop advances orders on Fyers futures quotes with the page closed; owner emails for fills, exits and a 15:40 summary. `indexFramework.ts` (tests `scripts/index-framework.test.mjs`) is the daily-regime (six checks) and hourly-setup checklist behind `GET /api/paper/index/signal?index=NIFTY`, with a sized proposal; the framework itself is unproven. Needs today's Fyers login (no futures on Yahoo).
- **Fyers quote time (14 Oct 2026, bug fixed).** Fyers' `/data/quotes` field `tt` is the trading DATE at 00:00 UTC, not a trade time, and there is no last-trade-time field. Treating it as one made every Fyers quote look hours old (so the stock paper engine would have rejected all fills and freshness labels showed stale). `tradeTime` in `fyersQuotes.ts` now stamps a quote dated today with the fetch time and an earlier day with that day's 15:30 IST close. Consequence: a Fyers outage that returns frozen prices is not detectable from the quote itself, and `feed.freshestQuoteAgeMs` only measures how old the session is, not feed latency.
- **Fyers live quotes provider (13 Oct 2026).** `MARKET_PROVIDER=fyers` selects `src/lib/market/providers/fyers.ts`: Fyers `/data/quotes` (50 symbols a call, shared throttle of 120 requests a minute, 2-second quote cache) while today's login is active, Yahoo for everything else (daily history, sparklines, symbols Fyers cannot quote, and the whole feed when not logged in). Its `id` is `fyers` only while connected and `yahoo` otherwise, so Yahoo-specific delay disclosures stay correct; `historyCacheId` stays `yahoo` so the 2,300-stock history cache is reused. Helpers and tests: `fyersQuotes.ts`, `scripts/fyers-quotes.test.mjs`. `/api/fyers/status` now returns `feed` stats (Fyers vs Yahoo-fallback quote counts, freshest quote age). Verified only on the Yahoo-fallback path; the live path needs a login at `/api/fyers/login` (tokens expire each IST day) and the field names follow Fyers' v3 docs from memory, so check `feed.fyersQuotes > 0` after the first login. No orders are ever placed.
- **Bottomed Out screener added (11 Oct 2026, experimental).** Rules in `src/lib/screen/bottomedOut.ts` (tests `scripts/bottomed-out.test.mjs`), backtest `scripts/backtest-bottom.mjs`, API `/api/market/bottomed-out` (`bottomedOutResults.ts`), page `BottomedOutScreener` (nav `bottomed`, `#bottomed-out`, Scanner tools menu and directory family "Reversals").
  - Rule: liquid, 35%+ below the 252-session high, 120-session low set 8-60 sessions ago, close 8-50% above it, last-5-session low more than 2% above the base low, close above the 20 EMA. Tier "deep" = 50%+ below the high.
  - Backtest (Oct 2024 - Oct 2026, next-open entry, 0.25% costs): all tiers -0.09R; early tier (35-50%) -0.13R; deep tier +0.11R over 397 trades with a fixed -8% stop / +16% target (about +0.10R with a base-low stop and 2R/3R targets, 0.00R with an EMA50 exit). Volume, EMA50, RSI divergence and breadth gates did not help consistently, so they are context only and never filter or rank.
  - Hourly email: "Bottomed out - deep base" section (deep tier, top 10, New/Unchanged tags, dropped line) via `addBottomedOut` in `hourlyEmail.ts`; state `lastBottomed`. Not in the subject, not in `hasChanges`, not in the pre-open email.
- **A breakout "near 52-week high" section was added to the pre-open email (2 Oct 2026).**
  - Logic lives in `src/lib/screen/highBreakout.ts` (tests in `scripts/high-breakout.test.mjs`). `getScannerResults` stores the result in `payload.highBreakouts` from liquid stocks' completed candles, and `buildPreOpenEmail(..., highBreakouts)` renders it under "52-week-high breakouts — experimental".
  - It is listed only when breadth is at least 50% (`highBreakoutsVisible`). Below that it shows a single "Hidden today" line with the counts.
  - It is labelled experimental and kept separate from Buy ready; it is not in the hourly email or the PNG.
  - Cards rank tight bases first, then volume. Each card states a −3% stop and an exit after a close below the 21 EMA. The caveat quotes the +0.09R result, made only in 2026.
- **52-week-high breakout method (Jaynesh Kasliwal webinar) is not adopted.** `scripts/backtest-jk-breakout.mjs` (run with `node --use-system-ca`) tests his Chartink screen (within 5% of the 52-week high, up over 65 days, EMA20 > EMA50, close > EMA21) with exact entry and exit rules. Breadth-gated rows only have about 2 years of usable data (Oct 2024 to Sep 2026). Results on 2 Oct 2026:
  - The raw screen and plain 20-day breakouts lose −0.16 to −0.20R. Requiring 1.5× or 2× volume, or a 65-day return above Nifty's, barely changes that.
  - Breadth ≥ 50% gives the biggest lift, to about −0.07R. A base range of 15% or less with an EMA21-close exit is best at +0.09R over 585 trades, but 2025 was flat; all of the gain came in 2026.
  - A fixed −3% stop with a +6–8% target loses in every variant.
- **Bullish confluence is not a ranking priority.** It was tested with the same swing plan on the three families that can be backtested (Trade Triggers, RPCI, Oscillators ≥ 8). Results:
  - 0 families: −0.13R.
  - 1 family: −0.14R.
  - 2 families: −0.13R, no better than any liquid stock (−0.13R).
  - 3 families: −0.01R, but only 98 trades.
  - Core Setups and RSI Edge have no history in the backtest.
  - Hourly email confluence tag (5 Oct 2026, user decision): every stock already in the hourly email (new Buy ready, still Buy ready, watch added/unchanged) shows "n/5 scanners" (or "scanners disagree") next to RS, with a footnote that it is context only. Built in `hourlyEmail.ts` `addConfluence` (screen route `GET` + live scanner payload + RSI Edge → `buildConfluence`) and `withConfluence` in `src/lib/alerts/hourlyConfluence.ts`; "/4" when RSI Edge is unavailable, no tags if the screen scan fails. It never adds, removes or reorders stocks. Pre-open email unchanged.
  - Hourly full lists + Bullish confluence section (5 Oct 2026, user decision, supersedes "changes only" for stock sections and "confluence not emailed"): `buildHourlyEmail` now repeats the **full** Buy ready (top 10) and watch (top 5) lists every hour as tables with a leading **Status** column (`STATUS_PILL`: New / Added / Unchanged / Was buy / Removed) against the baseline, plus struck-through Removed rows for lost buys/dropped watch stocks, so readers who missed an email still see everything. Text version uses `[Status] SYMBOL` lines. A separate section "Bullish confluence — where the scanners agree" (Top 10 · not a buy) lists `table.bullConfluence` from `topConfluence` (same as the app panel: `rankConfluence(map,"bull",2)`, no conflicts, turnover ≥ ₹5 Cr, 3+ families first), each with status New/Unchanged vs `lastConfluence` in `.cache/email-alert.json` (same day only) and a "Dropped out of the top 10" line. Confluence changes never count toward `hasChanges`. Never present it as a buy (no positive backtest). Pre-open email unchanged (it still uses `watchHtml`).
- **Shorts stay out of customer emails.**
  - Strong short (8/8) looked strong on all liquid stocks: +0.15R, positive in both halves.
  - On F&O stocks only (current list, data from Oct 2024), the result fell to +0.04R. It lost in 2025 (−0.13R), and without its 10 best symbols the total was −12.8R.
  - Re-test before adding shorts anywhere customer-facing.
- Shared alert formatting helpers can remain even if their historical filenames mention Telegram, because email generation still depends on them.

## Stock detail drawer

- `src/components/StockDetailDrawer.tsx` is the single place for per-stock analysis: candlestick chart (20/50/200 DMA, volume, entry/stop/targets/pivot), Buy horizon plans with every pass/fail check, Short rating checks, cross-workspace scanner matches, and base structure.
- Open it through `StockSymbolButton` / `useOpenStock` from `src/components/StockDetailContext.tsx`; `Dashboard.tsx` provides the context and renders the drawer. New tables must make the stock identity clickable with `StockSymbolButton`.
- The header search and command palette open the drawer; adding to the watchlist happens from the drawer button.
- `BuyingStatus` and `ShortSellingStatus` expose `checks` so UIs can show passed and failed checks.
- `ScanRow.fromHigh` is the positive percentage below the 52-week high (0 = at the high). Chartink scanner `values.fromHigh` uses the opposite, negative convention.
- Plan price lines do not stretch the price autoscale. A level outside the visible range shows only its axis label at the edge.

## Pro chart (TradingView Lightweight Charts, 30 September 2026)

- The drawer chart is `src/components/ProChart.tsx`, built on `lightweight-charts` v5 (the same library Scanner Pro uses). The old SVG chart was removed. The drawer loads 750 daily sessions (`MAX_HISTORY_CANDLES = 750` in `/api/market/history`).
- Features:
  - timeframes Daily/Weekly/Monthly, built by `src/lib/chart/aggregate.ts` (IST Monday weeks, calendar months);
  - ranges 3M/6M/1Y/All; Log and % scales; Reset; PNG export; `?` shortcuts panel;
  - overlays: MA 20/50/200, Bollinger, Supertrend (10,3), Ichimoku with a future cloud, classic pivots from the last completed higher-timeframe bar, Auto S/R, candle patterns, volume;
  - panes: RSI, MACD, Stochastic, ADX, ATR. Log/% scale modes apply to the price pane only; oscillator panes stay Normal;
  - drawing tools: trend line and horizontal line, with undo/redo/clear.
- TradingView-style look (2 Oct 2026):
  - filled candles in TradingView's `#089981`/`#f23645`; the symbol and timeframe as a watermark;
  - a top-left legend over the chart shows OHLC, change and every active overlay's inputs and values at the crosshair (the last bar when not hovering). Each oscillator pane has its own legend at the pane top (`paneTops`, measured from `IPaneApi.getHeight()`). Hovering a legend row shows ⚙ (settings) and ✕ (remove);
  - ⚙ opens an Inputs dialog for MA lengths, Bollinger, Supertrend, RSI length and Regression Breakout. Inputs live in `src/lib/chart/chartParams.ts` (`PARAM_DEFS`, clamped and snapped by `cleanParam`) and persist in `settings.params`. Indicator series are computed in the `ind` memo outside the build effect so the legend can read them;
  - "☾ Dark" forces a dark chart via `data-theme="dark"` on the wrapper while the app stays light; "⛶ Full screen" (F) uses the Fullscreen API on the wrapper, and the dialog renders inside it;
  - ARBM bands, map and trendlines use `autoscaleInfoProvider: () => null` so they do not stretch the price axis. Negative axis labels under the candles are the 20% volume margin, not a bug;
  - on rebuild, a saved zoom that showed the last bar is shifted by the number of new bars, so newly loaded history keeps the latest candle in view. A saved zoom is ignored after the symbol changes.
- Keyboard shortcuts:
  - D/W/M: timeframes;
  - arrows: pan and zoom;
  - Ctrl+L: log scale; Ctrl+P: % scale; Alt+R: reset;
  - T: trend line; H: horizontal line; Esc: cancel;
  - Ctrl+Z/Y: undo/redo; Ctrl+Shift+S: PNG; F: full screen.
- Settings persist in localStorage `traders-adda:chart`; drawings persist per symbol in `traders-adda:drawings` and are anchored by date, so they survive timeframe switches.
- The chart rebuilds only on structural changes. Plan levels (Entry/Stop/T1/T2/Pivot) move with the live scan poll, so they are patched as price lines in a separate effect. Never put per-tick props into the build effect: it resets hover and drawing state.
- Auto S/R (`src/lib/chart/autoLevels.ts`, `AUTO_LEVEL_RULES`):
  - swing pivots (3 bars; 2 on W/M) clustered within max(0.6 ATR, 0.5%);
  - at least 2 touches, within 25% of price, at most 3 levels per side;
  - flipped levels are marked ↺.
- Candle patterns (`src/lib/chart/candlePatterns.ts`, 15 patterns) are **off by default** and labelled "context only, no backtested edge". Evidence: `scripts/backtest-candle-patterns.mjs` (41,982 hits, 2022–2026) found about a 50% hit rate on 10-day excess return for every pattern. Do not use patterns in recommendations.
- Not possible with daily EOD data: VWAP, intraday timeframes, OI or order flow.
- Scanner Pro's live app blocks automated access (403 "Automated access is not permitted") and requires login. Do not spoof the user agent, log in, or automate the user's browser. Compare features using public information and user screenshots.
- Tests: `scripts/chart-lib.test.mjs`, `scripts/chart-params.test.mjs`.

## Unified status and Today's Picks (30 September 2026)

- Paper trading prototype: `#journal` now contains a browser-local paper portfolio separate from the manual Trade Journal. Approve only Buy ready stocks from **Last close** in Today's Picks (not provisional Live Session/watch); use the actual completed `candleTimestamp` as signal date, not the active `sessionDateKey` which may already be today. Snapshot the plan and size using `computePositionSize` at the worst allowed buy-zone price for at most 1% of starting paper capital at risk, limited by available paper cash. Poll live quote snapshots only while the tab is open/visible; reject stale, delayed, simulated-session and off-market quotes. No broker integration, no historical replay when offline, no claim that quote-observed fills replicate exchange execution. Paper entry/exit rules live in `src/lib/screen/paperTrading.ts`; `usePaperTrading` persists them under `sa.paperTrading.v1`. Report storage failures, and never intermingle paper orders with actual manual journal entries. The engine logs an event only when the status message changes (a 5 s poll would otherwise flood localStorage). `scripts/paper-replay.mjs SYMBOL ENTRY-DAY [capital] [--json]` (run with `node --use-system-ca`) replays the same engine on real Yahoo 5-minute bars for a past Buy ready alert-scanner signal (Yahoo keeps ~60 days); use it for demos on holidays/closed-gate days. `--until=`/`--cancel` stop or cancel the replay to show pending/open/cancelled states, and `--demo=FILE` appends the order with id prefix `demo-`; `isDemoPaperOrder` orders are badged DEMO, never polled, excluded from cash/P&L/duplicate checks, and removable via "Remove demo data". Each row has an expandable event timeline. Orders also carry `fills` (BUY at entry; SELLs labelled T1/T2/Stop/Time exit with time, qty, price); `upgradePaperOrder` rebuilds fills for orders saved before that field existed. The panel is broker-style: summary cards (cash, invested, current value, unrealized/realized P&L; summarizes demo orders only when no real orders exist), Positions & orders (order time, buy time × qty × price, amount invested, sells, holding at last price, P&L %), and a Trade book of every fill.
- One status per stock everywhere (`src/lib/screen/tradeStatus.ts`): **Buy ready** (every check passes, breadth included), **Watch** (only breadth fails, or a high risk flag caps it), **Extended** (only the extension check fails; breadth may too), **Avoid** (any other stock check fails), **Short ready** (every bearish check passes; research only, never emailed). `longStatusKey` and `combinedStatusKey` are the only rules; Strong watch / Developing / Weak / Strong short / Short watch no longer exist.
- PA rating, oscillator score, confluence, candle patterns and breakout stage are explanations only; they never change or compete with the status. Oscillator verdicts read "Strong vote/Bullish vote…", levels read "Price below trigger / In buy zone / Price above buy zone / Price below stop", breakout stage is a neutral grey tag.
- `TradeStatusBadge.tsx` holds the colours (emerald/sky/amber/slate/rose), `TradeStatusPill` and `TradeStatusLegend`; Buying/ShortSelling badges derive from it. Watchlist shows one Status column (combined) with a status filter; the drawer header shows one pill.
- Today's Picks (`#picks`, first under Overview, `TodaysPicks.tsx`) = `todaysPicks(payload)` in `src/lib/screen/todaysPicks.ts`: breadth gate >= 50% → Buy ready only from `ALERT_SCANNER_KEYS` rows (passesFloor + plan) plus gated RPCI/Oscillator extras → one entry per symbol (sources merged) → RS desc → top 5. Weak breadth: no picks, a separate "Strong stocks waiting for the market: not a buy" list (see `WATCH_RULES` above). Uses the whole-market scanner payload (universe filter not applied) and the scanner mode toggle: Last close = pre-open email, Live = hourly email.
- `buildAlertTable(..., { recommendationsOnly: true })` rows are exactly `todaysPicks().picks`, so the page and the customer emails always match. Keep them on the same function.
- PA is shown next to RS on Today's Picks, the pre-open email cards, the hourly/attachment images and Telegram (`paBrief`/`paText` in priceActionRating.ts; `ExtraPick.pa` is computed for RPCI/Oscillator extras). Display only, never used to rank.
- Selection backtest (30 September 2026, T1/T2 exit, 0.25% cost, daily top 5, 1st half / 2nd half): current rule (email scanners, Buy ready, RS) −0.02R (263 trades; −0.03 / 0.00). Ranking by PA instead: −0.03R, never better than RS. All 13 scanners by RS: +0.03R but unstable (−0.18 / +0.23). Email + leader + ath by RS: +0.04R (304; −0.01 / +0.08), the only variant better in both halves but on a small sample. Buying on weak-breadth days (checks pass except breadth): email scanners −0.22R, all 13 −0.09R, all 13 top 1 −0.02R, so the breadth gate is kept. PA grade on its own shows no edge (A+ −0.12R, A −0.05R).

## Today's Command Center

- Clickable metrics use `dashboardMetrics.ts` to show full exact membership in an inline, keyboard-accessible table with coverage. DMA lists include equality and reject nonfinite/missing values; advancing rejects nonfinite/flat changes. These three use `marketRows`, not universe-filtered rows. Buy ready selects only that status from the existing horizon-ranked research ideas; Short ready uses the existing F&O research list. Do not redirect these research counts to curated Today's Picks or truncate drilldowns to the top-eight research panels. Symbols open the shared stock drawer. Tests: `scripts/dashboard-metrics.test.mjs`.

- "Today" (`activeNav === "today"`, `src/components/CommandCenter.tsx`) is the default landing page and the logo target; the hash-sync fallback also goes there.
- Pure logic lives in `src/lib/screen/commandCenter.ts` (tests: `scripts/command-center.test.mjs`): `marketRegime` (risk-on: breadth50 ≥ 60 and breadth200 ≥ 50; risk-off: breadth50 < 40, or < 50 with breadth200 < 40), `rankBuyIdeas`, `nearestBuyIdeas`, `rankShortIdeas`, `groupScanBySector` (shared with Dashboard) and `sessionChanges`.
- Ideas require turnover ≥ ₹5 Cr. When no long idea is Buy ready or Watch, the panel shows the closest Extended/near-miss setups (Avoid with rating >= 60) under an amber "reference levels only" banner, never as entries.

## UI conventions (visual polish, 28 September 2026)

- Loading, empty and unavailable states use `LoadingState` (shimmer skeleton + message) and `EmptyState` (`tone`: neutral / search / error) from `src/components/WorkspaceShell.tsx`. Do not add ad-hoc "Loading…" paragraphs.
- Wide data tables follow the RSI Edge design: `border-separate border-spacing-0`, sticky `#` and Instrument columns, uppercase 10px headers on `#f7f9fa`, symbol + truncated name, mono right-aligned numbers.
- Striped rows must use opaque colours (`odd:bg-white even:bg-[#fafbfc] hover:bg-[#f0f9f4]`) because sticky cells use `bg-inherit`; translucent colours let scrolled content show through.
- Put long rule text and data-source metadata in a "Rules & data source" `<details>`, and row-level plans in an expandable row, not an absolutely positioned popover (it is clipped by the scroll container).
- Page switches animate with `.page-enter` (keyed on `activeNav` in Dashboard). `prefers-reduced-motion` disables `.page-enter` and `.skeleton`.
- Edit files containing ₹, ×, · or — with the edit tool or Node, never PowerShell 5 `Get-Content`/`Set-Content`, which double-encodes UTF-8.

## Scanner confluence

- Logic lives in `src/lib/screen/confluence.ts` (tests: `scripts/confluence.test.mjs`); badge in `src/components/ConfluenceBadge.tsx`.
- Confluence counts independent families, not scans: Core Setups, RPCI, Oscillators, Trade Triggers, RSI Edge (n/5). Two Core Setups count once.
- Bull: active Core Setup (played-out is muted), any RPCI stage, oscillator strong/bullish, visible Trade Trigger passing the liquidity floor (below floor muted; fall4 neutral as counter-trend), RSI Edge daily/weekly bullish. Bear: oscillator bearish, RSI Edge bearish.
- A stock with both bull and bear families is a conflict and is excluded from rankings. Levels: 3+ High confluence, 2 Confirmed, 1 Single scanner.
- Today shows Bullish/Bearish confluence panels (≥2 families, turnover ≥ ₹5 Cr, top 8); the drawer's Scanner matches card shows the badge. Dashboard loads scanners and RSI Edge on the Today view for this.

## RVOL and risk flags

- `src/lib/screen/riskFlags.ts` (tests: `scripts/risk-flags.test.mjs`); UI pieces `RvolPill` and `RiskFlagChips` in `src/components/RiskSignals.tsx`. Every scan row carries `rvol` and `riskFlags`.
- RVOL = session volume ÷ average of the prior 50 sessions. While the market is live it is projected with a U-shaped NSE intraday volume curve (`expectedVolumeShare`), shown with "~", and hidden before 5% of the session has passed.
- High flags: gap-up faded (gap ≥2%, gave back ≥ half), climax run (≥25% in 10 sessions). Cautions: extended (≥25% above 50 DMA, suppressed when climax), thin liquidity (₹5–10 Cr median turnover), light-volume breakout (fresh breakout on <1.2× volume).
- `withRiskFlags` (buyingStatus.ts) caps Buy ready at Watch when any high flag is present; the rating % is unchanged. It is applied in `currentScanBuyingStatus`, all three horizon signals and Core Setups' `dashboardBuyingStatus`, and `BuyingStatusBadge` shows a red ⚠ line.
- Shown in: the Core Setups table ("Relative volume (RVOL)" measure, default on Breakouts/Climbing, plus flag chips), the drawer (RVOL KPI and a Risk flags card), Today (RVOL under the status/confluence badge, high flags on bullish confluence) and the Watchlist (under Volume).
- Inspired by Scanner Pro (scanner.mrchartist.com). Next candidates agreed from that review: rule text on scanner cards (done — see Scanner directory), new scans (52-week high on volume, 20 EMA pullback), true-cross alerts.

## Scanner directory

- `src/lib/screen/scannerDirectory.ts` (tests: `scripts/scanner-directory.test.mjs`) is the single catalogue of every visible scanner: family, one-line rule, direction (bull / bear / counter-trend / experimental), Buy horizon and navigation target. `TRADING_STYLES` maps horizons to tags: short = Swing (2–15 sessions), mid = Swing / positional (3–12 weeks), long = Positional (3–12+ months).
- `directoryCounts` counts unique symbols: Core Setups exclude played-out rows (rows + extraRows, so it can be slightly below the Core Setups stage-card totals, which count rows); Trade Triggers count liquid hits only; RSI Edge shows "Chartink source unavailable" on a per-scanner error and never guesses a rule.
- `ScannerDirectory` renders the cards at the bottom of Today; clicking opens the workspace (Trade Triggers open the exact scanner via `scanner-<key>` targets). `StyleTag` is also shown on the Trade Trigger Conditions card and next to the selected Core Setup criteria.
- Targets: RSI Edge cards use `rsi-edge-<key>` (Dashboard sets `RsiEdgeScannerSection initialTab`), oscillator cards use `signals-momentum` (scrolls to `momentum-title`).
- Full-app QA open items: drawer can't remove from watchlist; no URL/back-button state per workspace; Watchlist "Entry zone" header clipped by sticky column; raw Trade Triggers show negative backtest expectancy; Filters text says "BananaPatterns-style"; index page uses a different design and says "Live" when the market is closed.
- Breadth is market-wide, so rows never repeat it: `splitFailedChecks` (buyingStatus.ts) drives the badges' "Missing:" line (stock checks only; "Waits for market breadth" when breadth is the sole gap), and Trade Trigger "Fails:" omits it. Trade Triggers open on the strictest non-empty filter (Buy ready → Watch → All screener hits; chips Buy ready / Watch / Extended / Avoid / All) until the user picks one; the breadth banner says which list is shown.
- When adding or hiding a scanner, update `SCANNER_DIRECTORY` too; the test asserts it lists exactly `VISIBLE_SCANNER_KEYS` and `RSI_EDGE_SCAN_KEYS`.

## Universe picker (adopted from Scanner Pro, 29 September 2026)

- Header `UniversePicker` (Dashboard.tsx): All NSE / Nifty 50 / 100 / 200 / 500 / F&O stocks. Persisted in localStorage `traders-adda:universe` via `useUniverse`. Shown only on Today, Core Setups, RPCI & Oscillators, Trade Triggers and RSI Edge. Watchlist, Market, Breakouts and the drawer stay unfiltered. A green banner with "Show all NSE" appears while a filter is active.
- Membership lives in `src/lib/market/data/index-universes.json`, refreshed by `npm run update-universe` (niftyindices constituent CSVs + NSE `fo_mktlots.csv`, filtered to the EQ master). Read it through `indexUniverses.ts` (`universePredicate`, `universeSize`, `isFnO`). Pure filter logic is in `src/lib/screen/universeFilter.ts` (node-testable, no JSON import).
- It is a view filter only (no rescan). Breadth and regime must stay market-wide: `filterScan` keeps the unfiltered rows in `scan.marketRows`, and every client-side breadth calculation uses `scan.marketRows ?? scan.rows`. RSI Edge membership still comes only from Chartink; the filter only narrows it.
- Today's short ideas are always F&O-only (cash shorts must close the same day). The drawer shows an "F&O" chip and an amber note in the Short card for non-F&O stocks.
- Header: at widths below xl the "Universe" / "Quick actions" labels and the member count are hidden and the search keeps `min-w-[200px]`. Adding header items previously squeezed search to ~50px.

## Market Pulse card (Scanner Pro style, 29 September 2026)

- Pure logic lives in `src/lib/screen/marketPulse.ts` and is tested in `scripts/market-pulse.test.mjs`. The UI is `src/components/MarketPulseCard.tsx`, which replaced the old regime guidance panel in CommandCenter (Today).
- Score (0–100): 40% share above the 50 DMA, 30% share above the 200 DMA, 30% advance %. Weights are renormalised over the inputs that are available. The score is null when there is no data.
- Mood bands: bullish ≥65, constructive ≥55, neutral ≥45, cautious ≥35, else bearish.
- Stance comes from the regime:
  - risk-on → Press longs
  - selective → Be selective (breadth50 ≥ 50) or Build watchlist (breadth50 < 50)
  - risk-off → Defend capital
  - no data → Stand aside
- The card adds counter-trend notes for a bounce during risk-off and a dip during risk-on, a "Tape favours" line naming the top 2 sectors, and a collapsible signals breakdown.
- Mood (score) and headline (regime) can differ, e.g. "Cautious" alongside "Risk-off market". This is expected; the breakdown explains it.

## Breakout state chips on Core Setups (Scanner Pro style, 29 September 2026)

- Pure logic lives in `src/lib/screen/breakoutState.ts` and is tested in `scripts/breakout-state.test.mjs`. Each lifecycle tab gets a finer state:
  - Forming: Coiled (≥ −3% from the pivot and ATR ratio ≤ 0.75; unknown/0 coil never counts as coiled), Near pivot (≥ −5%), Building.
  - Fresh breakouts and Climbing: In buy zone (≤ +5% over the pivot), Extended (> +5%), Strong (≥ +20%).
  - Played out: Paid off (result > 0), Failed (hit the 8% stop), Faded (below the 50D without a gain).
- LivePatternSection shows a "Breakout state" chip row with counts after the stage rules. The filter is kept per tab. The row and card status badge is `BreakoutStateBadge`, which replaced the old `getCardStatus` text; each chip and badge has a tooltip with its rule.
- In the "Now vs pivot" pill, breakouts and climbing more than 5% over the pivot are amber (extended).

## Sector heatmap (Market → "Sector heatmap", 29 September 2026)

- Pure logic lives in `src/lib/screen/sectorHeatmap.ts` and is tested in `scripts/sector-heatmap.test.mjs`. The UI is `src/components/SectorHeatmap.tsx`, which replaced the old "The map" tile grid in `MarketPanel` (Dashboard.tsx).
- It uses the unfiltered `scan.rows`. Sectors are macro NSE sectors with at least `MIN_SECTOR_MEMBERS` stocks; symbols are de-duplicated and unclassified stocks are skipped.
- Metric toggle, each on a −3…+3 level scale:
  - 1-day move: sector average; levels at ±0.25 / 1 / 2%.
  - Above 50-day line: sector share above the 50D, centred on 50 with ±5 / 15 / 25 steps; for a stock, its distance from the 50D (±1 / 5 / 10%).
  - RS rating: sector median, centred on 50.
- Layout: tiles are ordered by traded value. The top 2 sectors get 2×2 tiles that also list their 4 largest stocks; the next 4 get 2×1. Clicking a sector opens a member heat grid (48 largest, with "Show all"); clicking a stock opens the drawer via `useOpenStock`.
- Colour steps: emerald 600/500/100 and red 100/500/600. These work in both themes; avoid red-700, which the dark theme remaps to a light colour.

## Dark/light theme (29 September 2026)

- The header ☾/☀ `ThemeToggle` (Dashboard.tsx) uses `useTheme` (`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`). The theme is the `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`, persisted in localStorage `traders-adda:theme`. An inline script in `layout.tsx` applies it before first paint; `<html>` has `suppressHydrationWarning`.
- Dark mode works by remapping Tailwind v4 palette variables under `[data-theme="dark"]` in `globals.css`:
  - `--color-white`, the slate scale, and the accent hues (light tints become dark tints, and the 700–950 steps become light).
  - Components need no `dark:` classes.
  - Elements that are dark in both themes are pinned explicitly (`bg-slate-900`, `text-white`, `from-slate-950`, `bg-white/10`, …).
- Arbitrary hex classes (e.g. `bg-[#e7f6ee]`) compile to literals, so each one needs an escaped override in the dark block. Prefer palette classes in new code. Do not add unlayered overrides for common base classes, because they beat `hover:` utilities.
- Literal SVG colours must use `style={{ stroke/fill: "var(--chart-grid)" | "var(--chart-surface)" | "var(--accent)" }}` so charts follow the theme (drawer, LivePatternSection, IndexAnalysisPage).
- Verify both themes with headless Edge via `playwright-core` (`chromium.launch({ channel: "msedge" })`), setting localStorage in `addInitScript`. The integrated browser's screenshots are often stale.

## Navigation shell and page headers (Scanner Pro style, 29 September 2026)

**Sidebar**
- Width is 248px, or 72px when collapsed.
- Always dark. It uses the literal-colour `.sidenav*` classes at the end of `globals.css`, not Tailwind palette classes, which would flip in dark mode.
- Groups:

**Header**
- 60px tall.

**Clocks**

**`WorkspaceHero`** (WorkspaceShell.tsx)
- Light and theme-aware: white surface, a 3px emerald gradient strip at the top, an optional `icon` tile (a `NavIconName`), an emerald eyebrow, a slate-900 title and a slate-500 description.
