- Never use `text-white`, `bg-white/10` or `text-*-200/300` there.

## Unrated stocks

- A stock is rated only with ≥20 daily sessions (`computeMetrics`) and when it passes `LIQUIDITY_FLOOR` (₹500 Cr mcap, ₹5 Cr median turnover). Short-history symbols are listed in `scan.insufficientHistory`.
- `src/lib/screen/unrated.ts` (`unratedReason`, tests in `scripts/unrated.test.mjs`) explains why a stock has no rating; the drawer shows a "Recently listed — not rated yet" card with listing open, change since listing and high/low since listing, or the liquidity-floor/no-data reason.

## Morning brief (Today, 30 September 2026)

- Pure logic lives in `src/lib/screen/morningBrief.ts` (tests: `scripts/morning-brief.test.mjs`); the UI is `src/components/MorningBriefCard.tsx`, rendered above `MarketPulseCard` in CommandCenter.
- Data comes from `src/lib/market/globalCues.ts` through `/api/market/global-cues` and the `useGlobalCues` hook (5-minute cache and poll). It calls Yahoo directly because global indices, futures, yields and FX are not in the NSE instrument master the provider maps against.
- Two sections of a typical broker brief cannot be sourced and must never be faked:
  - GIFT Nifty has no free feed. The card shows a *derived* opening bias — a weighted average of the overnight tape (`BIAS_WEIGHTS`), with Brent and USD/INR inverted — and the summary always says it is computed, not quoted.
  - NSE's `api/option-chain-indices` is bot-protected (HTTP 404 behind Akamai). Key levels are classic floor pivots off the previous session's range for Nifty, Bank Nifty and Sensex, labelled as price structure, not OI walls.
- Broker recommendation lists are not reproduced. The "What qualifies today" list is this workstation's own `rankBuyIdeas` output for the selected horizon, and says "watchlist day" when nothing is Buy ready or Watch. `ideasLoading` keeps that message from appearing while the universe scan is still warming.
- Yahoo's `meta.chartPreviousClose` is the close *before* the requested range, not the prior session, so `toCue` takes the previous close from `candles.at(-2)`. Using the meta field reported a 5-day move as a 1-day move.
- `previousSession` drops an in-progress candle via `excludeDateKey` so levels never come from a half-formed bar.
- Cue colours follow the effect on Indian equities: cues flagged `inverseTone` (crude, USD/INR, the dollar index, the US 10-year, India VIX) read red when they rise.
- "Copy brief" writes `formatMorningBriefText`, which carries the same disclaimers plus "Scanner output, not investment advice."

## Pre-open brief email (09:00 IST, 30 September 2026)

- The same brief is emailed once per trading day at **09:00 IST**, 15 minutes before the open. Formatter: `src/lib/alerts/preOpenEmailFormat.ts` (tests: `scripts/preopen-email.test.mjs`); orchestration and scheduler: `src/lib/alerts/preOpenEmail.ts`; manual trigger and preview: `/api/alerts/preopen`.
- Gated by `PREOPEN_EMAIL_AUTO_SEND=1`, separate from the hourly email's `EMAIL_AUTO_SEND`, so either can run without the other. Both schedulers start from `src/instrumentation.ts`.
- **It is the inverse of the hourly email.** The hourly mail warns that an incomplete candle may revise its numbers; this one reads from `getScannerResults("completed")` and states that levels and ideas are final. Never reuse `hourlyEmailPreview()` here — it hardcodes `"live"`.
- `preOpenSlotKey` gives one `YYYY-MM-DD:preopen` slot per trading day, valid only between 09:00 and 09:15 IST, de-duplicated through `.cache/preopen-email.json`. It checks `isTradingDay()` rather than the market phase, because `MARKET_FORCE_LIVE=1` pins the phase to `OPEN` and would otherwise silence the email permanently in development. `isTradingDay` in `marketHours.ts` deliberately ignores that dev flag.
- The slot key is captured *before* the universe warm-up, which can run past 09:15; otherwise the day's send would be recorded against a null slot.
- A cue-feed outage degrades rather than cancels: the macro section empties and the feed is listed under "Unavailable this morning", but the levels and ideas still ship.
- The shared `table.footer` risk and advice lines are filtered out because the email states both in its own words; stops wider than 6% carry a ⚠ marker, which that footer promises.
- **No attachment.** The morning brief is read in place; the ideas PNG (`renderEmailTablePng`) belongs to the hourly alert, where the table is the whole message. Do not reintroduce it here.
- **Sender identity:** recipients see `EMAIL_FROM_NAME` ("Traders Adda") beside `EMAIL_FROM`. The address must be one the SMTP account may send as — Gmail silently rewrites the From header back to `SMTP_USER` for any unverified alias (confirmed in testing: a `noreply@tradersadda.com` From arrived as the Gmail address), and a domain that is not owned fails SPF/DKIM and lands in spam. The brand name is the supported way to show "Traders Adda"; `emailConfig` strips quotes and newlines from it so it cannot break out of the header.
- **The HTML is customer-facing, so it follows email-client rules, not web rules:** a 640px `role="presentation"` table layout, every style inline (a `<style>` block only carries the mobile media query, which Outlook ignores), no flexbox/grid/`float`, and `width="640"` kept as an attribute for Outlook while the inline style is `width:100%;max-width:640px` so phones do not overflow.
- Ideas render as one card per stock with a stacked Buy above / Stop loss / Targets metric row, not a 7-column table — a wide table is unreadable on a phone. Cue cards are two per row and levels three per row; all carry `class="col"`, which the media query turns into full-width blocks under 620px.
- `row.status` is `"buy" | "watch" | "weak"` (see `PickStatus`), **not** `"buy-ready"`. The status pill colours off those values; an earlier `"buy-ready"` comparison was silently always false and was caught by `tsc`, so keep test fixtures typed to the real union.
- A hidden preheader div supplies the inbox preview line; `color-scheme: light only` stops mail clients inverting the palette.

## Index Scalp Desk (`/scalp`, decided 5 October 2026)

- User decisions: data from **Fyers API v3** (free; user picked it over Zerodha/Upstox/Dhan/Angel), charts with **TradingView Lightweight Charts** (not the licensed Advanced Charts or TV widgets), **our own indicators and signals**. Yahoo cannot serve this: no NSE option data and only ~7 days of 1m bars.
- Files: `src/lib/scalp/scalpLogic.ts` (pure: `ema`, per-IST-day `vwap`, `openingRange`, `orbSignals`, `parseChain`, `pickLeg`, `futuresSymbol`, `parseCandles`; tests in `scripts/scalp-logic.test.mjs`), `src/lib/fyers/fyersClient.ts` (server-only; env `FYERS_APP_ID`/`FYERS_SECRET_ID`/`FYERS_REDIRECT_URI`, default redirect `http://127.0.0.1:3107/api/fyers/callback`; token in `.cache/fyers-token.json`, valid only on the IST day issued; requests paced ≥150 ms apart and ≤120/min on a `globalThis` pacer because 3 per-minute breaches block the user for the day; auth codes -8/-15/-16/-17 or 401 clear the token → `FyersAuthError`; browser User-Agent required), `src/lib/scalp/desk.ts` (`getScalpDesk`: chain cached 20 s, desk 8 s, in-flight dedupe; history fetched sequentially), routes `api/fyers/login` (state cookie on the redirect URI's origin), `api/fyers/callback`, `api/fyers/status` (GET; DELETE = disconnect), `api/scalp/desk?index=NIFTY|BANKNIFTY&offset=-3..3` (401 when not connected), UI `src/app/scalp/page.tsx` → `components/scalp/ScalpDesk.tsx` + `ScalpChart.tsx` (times shifted +19800 s so the axis reads IST; data updated in place so zoom survives polling). Sidebar "Index Scalp Desk" in `Dashboard.tsx`.
- Index spot has no volume: VWAP comes from the futures (status tile) and from each option's own volume.
- **Stock drawer chart uses Fyers when logged in** (user asked 5 Oct 2026): `useFyersChartCandles` → `GET /api/fyers/candles?symbol=&sessions=750` → `getFyersDailyCandles` in `src/lib/fyers/fyersCandles.ts` (tries `NSE:SYM-EQ`, then `-BE`/`-SM`/`-ST`; ≤365-day chunks; daily bars re-stamped from IST midnight to 09:15 IST like Yahoo; 5-min cache). Only `ProChart` gets these candles; ratings, levels, timeframe agreement and unrated stats keep using the scan's Yahoo candles so they match the scanners. A caption under the chart names the source; with no Fyers login it falls back to Yahoo. Scanners/emails stay on Yahoo: they must run unattended (Fyers needs a daily manual login) and a full-universe rescan would hit Fyers' 200/min limit.
- **Intraday chart timeframes (Fyers only, 5 Oct 2026)**: `ProChart` prop `intraday` (drawer passes `fyersCandles != null`) adds 1m/5m/15m/1h buttons (`src/lib/chart/intraday.ts`: 5/30/60/100 days requested). `useFyersIntradayCandles` → `/api/fyers/candles?resolution=1|5|15|60` → `getFyersIntradayCandles` (30 s cache, raw bar-open ms). Polls every 30 s 09:15–15:31 IST weekdays and keeps the last good bars on error. Chart times are UTC timestamps shifted +19800 s so the axis shows IST. Pivots on intraday use the previous completed daily bar; range buttons are hidden; daily-drawn drawings older than the intraday window are skipped. Without Fyers, a saved intraday timeframe falls back to Daily.
- The ORB markers are **display-only "Not proven · see backtest"**. Do not present them as trades, automate them or add live orders unless a 1-minute backtest after costs shows an edge, then paper trading; live orders only on explicit user request and within SEBI's retail-algo framework (trading app + static IP).
- **ORB backtest (5 Oct 2026)**: `/scalp/backtest` → `GET /api/scalp/backtest?days=365` → `getScalpBacktest` in `src/lib/scalp/backtestRun.ts` (fixed 90-day windows of 1-min spot + continuous futures, `cont_flag=1`; completed windows cached on disk in `.cache/scalp-history/`; report memoised 10 min). Pure engine `src/lib/scalp/backtest.ts` (`backtestOrb`, `simulateTrade`, `roundTripCost`, `summarize`, `verdictOf`; tests `scripts/scalp-backtest.test.mjs`). Rules: replays `orbSignals` per day with the previous day for EMA warm-up; entry next bar open; stop checked before target in a bar; gaps fill at the open; square-off 15:20. Option P&L = 0.5 delta × points × lot (Nifty 65, Bank Nifty 30); costs ≈ ₹131/₹132 per lot round trip (₹20/order brokerage, exchange 0.0355%, SEBI, GST 18%, STT 0.15% sell (conservative), stamp, slippage ₹0.5/₹1 premium per side) ≈ 4.0 / 8.8 index points. "Edge" requires ≥100 trades, positive net per trade and both halves positive. Fyers has no history for expired options or futures contracts, so the option-VWAP filter is untested. **Result 6 Oct 2025 – 5 Oct 2026: no edge after costs for either index and every variant** (Nifty 523 trades, −₹82.7k/lot; Bank Nifty 512 trades, +₹18.8k gross, −₹48.8k net; the best variant, "1 trade a day", was still −₹28k / −₹6.6k). So do not build paper or live auto-trading on this ORB; a new strategy would need its own backtest first.
- **Setup comparison (5 Oct 2026, same engine)**: `src/lib/scalp/setups.ts` (`SETUPS`: ORB; `vwapPullbackSignals` = futures on one side of VWAP for 18 of the last 20 min, EMA21 sloping that way over 10 bars, futures bar touches VWAP ±0.03% and closes on the trend side, spot bar closes in the trend direction, 09:45–14:30, 3/day, 20-min cooldown, 1× stop, 1.5R, 20-min exit; `pdhPdlSignals` = 1-min close crosses previous-day high/low with futures on the same side of VWAP, 09:30–14:30, one per side, 1× stop, 2R, 30-min exit; `trend5mSignals` = completed 5-min bar (aligned to 09:15) with an EMA 9/21 cross, close beyond EMA9, futures agree, 09:45–14:30, 3/day, 1.5× stop, 2R, 45-min exit). Generic runner `backtestSignals(input, detect, exits, costs)` (one trade at a time; `backtestOrb` wraps it with identical results). Rules were fixed before the first run; do not tune them to the results (multiple-testing bias). Tests in `scripts/scalp-setups.test.mjs`. **Result: no setup passed.** Net per lot: Nifty ORB −82.7k, VWAP −41.5k, PDH/PDL −8.5k, 5m trend −9.7k; Bank Nifty ORB −48.8k, VWAP −25.7k, PDH/PDL −15.4k, 5m trend +3.7k but the first half was −7.1k ("Not consistent"). Pattern: longer-hold trend rules beat fast scalps before costs, but costs (≈4/8.8 index pts per trade) erase it. The report UI is `src/components/scalp/ScalpBacktest.tsx` (comparison table plus per-setup tabs).
- **Longer holds (5 Oct 2026)**: `src/lib/scalp/holds.ts`, tests `scripts/scalp-holds.test.mjs`. Priced as one index-futures lot (`FUTURES_COSTS`: delta 1, ₹20/order, exchange 0.00173%, STT 0.05% sell, stamp 0.002%, slippage 1/3 pts per side; `roundTripCost(c, price)` uses the entry price) ≈ ₹1,000–1,050 / ₹1,150–1,200 per lot ≈ 15–16 / 38–40 index pts. Options are not used because theta can't be measured without option history. Intraday holds (1-min data, stop 1.5× base, no target, exit 15:15, min 100 trades): `firstHourBreakoutSignals` (60-min ORB, 1/day, by 13:00) and `trendHoldSignals` (first 5-min trend signal before 13:00). Swings (10 years of Fyers daily index data, cache `…-D-…json`, signal on the close, entry next open, stop 1.5×ATR14, gaps fill at the open, exit at the 3rd day's close, futures carry 6.5%/yr charged to longs and credited to shorts, min 50 trades): `breakout20Signals` (close beyond the prior 20-day high/low) and `rsi2Signals` (above SMA200 with RSI(2)<10 → long; below it with RSI(2)>90 → short; also exits on the first close beyond SMA5). `SetupResult` now carries `group`, `instrument`, `from/to/sessions/costPerTrade/costPoints`; the UI shows Long/Short for futures and a by-year grid for swings. **Result: none passed.** Net per lot: Nifty first-hour −184k, trend hold −86k, 20-day breakout −720k (10 yrs), RSI(2) −101k; Bank Nifty first-hour −197k, trend hold −92k, RSI(2) −241k, 20-day breakout +81k but second half −59k ("Not consistent"; PF 1.05). Do not automate any of these.
- **Option selling + trend following (5 Oct 2026)**: `src/lib/scalp/premium.ts` (tests `scripts/scalp-premium.test.mjs`): `bsPrice` (Black-Scholes, r 6.5%), `scheduledExpiry`/`actualExpiry` (Nifty weekly Thu → Tue from 1 Sep 2025; Bank Nifty weekly Wed until 13 Nov 2024, then monthly last Thu → last Tue from Sep 2025; holidays → previous session), `tradingYears` (time in trading days: sessions left + (1 − overnight share) × rest of today / 252), `overnightShare` (gap variance / close-to-close variance from daily bars, ≈42% Nifty, 36% Bank Nifty), `realisedVolByDay`/`ivRatioByDay` (Bank Nifty IV = VIX × 20-day realised-vol ratio, clamped 0.8–2), `shortLegCost`, `backtestStraddle` (sell ATM CE+PE at the 09:20 open, per-leg stop checked on the bar's worst index level + VIX high, gaps fill at open, buy back at 15:15; each leg = one trade). Data: 730 days of 1-min spot and `NSE:INDIAVIX-INDEX` (cache key `INDIAVIX`). The first calendar-time model lost before costs; switched to trading time (stated in the report's assumptions). Verdict override: if it passes but the "Premiums 10% cheaper" stress variant loses → "Model-sensitive". **Result: Nifty +₹52k, Bank Nifty +₹1.63L modelled, but the 5% and 10% stress rows lose ₹4–19L → Model-sensitive; only paper trading with live option quotes can confirm.** `trendFollow` in `holds.ts` (modes longShort/longOnly/price200/buyHold; switch at the next open; one extra round trip per month boundary for rolls; carry 6.5%): 50/200 long-short Nifty −₹4.28L, Bank Nifty −₹5.05L; long-or-flat −₹1.22L / −₹1.39L; buy-and-hold +₹3.67L / +₹3.83L. Trend following does not beat buy-and-hold. UI groups: "Option selling" and "Positional trend" (short call/put labels, cost note, by-year grid).
- **Filtered straddle + iron condor (5 Oct 2026)**: `premium.ts` adds `StraddlePlan.minIvOverRv` / `StraddleInput.realisedVol` (skip days where entry IV ÷ prior-20-session realised vol < threshold), `CondorPlan`/`DEFAULT_CONDOR`/`condorStrikes`/`backtestCondor` (4 legs, one VIX for all strikes = no skew, one stop on the whole position at `stopX` × credit checked at the bar high and low, `hold` "day" or "expiry" spanning sessions, stress = shorts × scale and wings ÷ scale, each position = a CE call-spread trade + a PE put-spread trade) and `dayStats` (legs per entry day combined → `SetupResult.dayStats`, shown as Winning/Worst/Best day/Per day on selling cards). `backtestRun.ts`: setups `STRADDLE_IVRV` (filter 1.2) and `CONDOR_920`; `flagModelSensitive` applies the 10%-stress override to all selling setups. Rules were fixed before the run. Results: filtered straddle Nifty −₹10.6k, Bank Nifty +₹50.8k but second half −₹13.3k (filter doesn't help); condor Nifty −₹1.09L (+₹1.30L before costs; ~₹487 of costs a day), Bank Nifty −₹2.30L. Post-hoc variants that looked good (expiry-day-only condor Nifty +₹19.7k, 82% win, 103 days; held to expiry +₹24.5k) are hypotheses only. Tests in `scripts/scalp-premium.test.mjs` (10).
- **Capital and return (5 Oct 2026)**: `SetupResult.capital` (`Capital`: blocked, basis, needed = blocked + maxDrawdown, endValue, returnPct = net ÷ needed, perYearPct = simple, years = sessions/252) set by `withCapital` at the end of `runIndex`; `result()`/`flagModelSensitive` work on `Draft` (= SetupResult without capital). Blocked: scalps = `bsPrice` ATM call × lot at last spot/VIX with `SCALP_SESSIONS_TO_EXPIRY` (Nifty 2.5, Bank Nifty 10); futures/straddle/condor = `MARGIN_PCT` 12%/15%/3% of last spot × lot. Shown in the "Strategy ranking" list (`Comparison` in `ScalpBacktest.tsx`: all setups of both indexes sorted by `tierOf` (0 passed, 1 profitable but Model-sensitive, 2 profitable but unproven, 3 lost money) then `capital.perYearPct`; index filter, hide-losers toggle; responsive rows: cards below `lg`, aligned grid columns from `lg` via `lg:contents`; clicking a row selects the setup tab and scrolls to `#setup-details`) and a money panel on each setup card.
- **Paper straddle (5 Oct 2026)**: `/scalp/paper` → `GET /api/scalp/paper` (refreshes at most once a minute when Fyers is connected; always returns the stored record) → `src/lib/scalp/paperStraddleRun.ts` (store `.cache/paper-straddle.json`, atomic write; `startPaperStraddleScheduler` registered in `src/instrumentation.ts`, ticks every 5 min on weekdays from 09:21 IST: refreshes every tick until 15:30 (today's day shows as "open" with live P&L), then retries every 10 min until 23:00 until both indexes are closed for today). For each session in the last 40 days whose nearest contract (`actualExpiry`) has not expired: ATM strike = 09:20 spot open rounded to 50/100; CE/PE symbols from `options-chain-v3` (strikecount 40, nearest expiry); legs replayed from the real contract 1-minute history (Fyers keeps live contracts' history back to listing, so the current cycle backfills); model sale price from `bsPrice` + VIX at 09:20 + `tradingYears` for "Real ÷ model". Pure logic `src/lib/scalp/paperStraddle.ts` (`replayLeg`, `priceDay`, `summarizePaper`, `PAPER_DAYS_NEEDED` = 40; tests `scripts/scalp-paper.test.mjs`). Never places orders. First backfill (30 Sep–5 Oct 2026): Nifty real/model 1.04×, net −₹2.2k over 3 days; Bank Nifty real/model 0.87× (the modelled Bank Nifty IV is too high, so its backtest profit is likely overstated), net −₹7.8k.

## Validation expectations

- Read the relevant Next.js 16.3.5 documentation under `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before changing Next.js APIs or conventions.
- For scanner changes, run focused scanner/alert tests, `npx tsc --noEmit`, targeted ESLint, and `npm run build`.
- For workspace UI changes, browser-check every sidebar destination, tab switching, sticky/internal table scrolling, and assert `document.body.scrollWidth === document.body.clientWidth`.
- Production is normally served at `http://localhost:3107` with `node --use-system-ca`.
- The full NSE universe can take several minutes to warm after a server restart; temporary HTTP 503 responses from market scan endpoints during warm-up are expected.

## Market strip, breadth and New/Dropped tags
- `MarketStrip` (top of every page, after `FyersBanner`) shows the market mode (`marketMode` in `src/lib/screen/breadthHistory.ts`, same thresholds as the Buy ready gate via `regimeKeyFor`), the share of liquid stocks above the 10/20/50/200-day averages, advance/decline, the price source and quote age, and an expandable 50-day breadth trend. Data: `/api/market/breadth` (history is recomputed from the universe candles per snapshot, ~130 sessions; today uses the forming candle while open).
- Mode is a size hint only ("Normal size" / "Reduce size" / "No new longs"); the paper engines do not read it yet.
- New/Dropped tags: `useListChanges(listId, symbols|null)` compares with the last earlier day the browser opened the page (localStorage, per browser, per list and scan mode). Silent on the first day. Applied to Today's Picks (buy and watch) and Bottomed Out.

## Weekly Top 5, scanner edge, owner alerts
- Weekly Top 5 (`src/lib/screen/weeklyTop5.ts`, `weeklyTop5Results.ts`, `/api/market/weekly-top5?limit=N`, `WeeklyTop5.tsx` on Today and Today's Picks): RS >= 80, 50>150>200-day stacked, within 25% of the 52-week high, stop 2 x ATR(14), 3R target, ranked by RS (scanner count breaks ties). The size note (`top5Size`) follows breadth: 60%+ normal, 50-60% quarter/paper, under 50% paper only. Evidence: scripts/backtest-gate-stops.mjs, backtest-criteria-check.mjs, backtest-sector-weak.mjs, backtest-weak-shorts.mjs, backtest-leaders.mjs (about 22 months, one cycle; the only robust edge was the 60% breadth gate).
- Scanner edge badges (`src/lib/screen/scannerEdge.ts`) come from the "BY BREADTH" section of scripts/backtest-scanners.mjs; update the table when that is re-run.
- Pre-open email carries the Top 5 on the first trading day of the week (`isFirstTradingDayOfWeek`), always in a test email, and in the browser preview with `/api/alerts/preopen?html=1&top5=1`.
- Owner-only Top 5 alerts (`top5Alert.ts`, rules in `top5AlertRules.ts`): market tier change (two readings in a row) and, after the close, a changed list (not while paper-only). State in `.cache/top5-alert.json`.

## Market cap data and the liquidity floor
- `src/lib/market/data/market-caps.json` (crore rupees, about 97% of the NSE list) comes from `node --use-system-ca scripts/fetch-market-caps.mjs` (Yahoo batch quote with a crumb). Re-run weekly; very new listings have none and pass the market-cap check by default. `universe.ts` merges it into `marketCapCr` ahead of the curated approximations.
- `LIQUIDITY_FLOOR` in `src/lib/screen/metrics.ts` is market cap >= ₹300 Cr and median turnover >= ₹5 Cr (was ₹500 Cr, but unenforced because most stocks had no market cap). The turnover floor is the next thing to revisit: BananaPatterns uses ₹1 Cr, and our liquidity-band backtest showed no benefit from ₹5 Cr.
- `globals.css` imports Tailwind with `source("../")` so only `src` is scanned. Do not remove it: browser profiles and caches under `tmp/` and `.cache/` once crashed the build with a 4 GB allocation failure.

## Nested bases on the screens
- A stock can be building several bases (levels 1 to 4). `walkEpisodes().bases` lists every born one; `StockMetrics.formingBases` measures them innermost first. The scan route lists a stock on a screen if any base passes: the innermost base is the main row, and a screen only an outer base satisfies gets an extra `forming` row keyed `SYMBOL|forming|L<level>` (`judgeBases` in `multiBase.ts`). Under a live breakout, an outer base still above the price counts as forming.
- Counts are compared with BananaPatterns in `docs/bananapatterns-comparison.md` sections 7 to 9.

## Screen floor, played out
- Two floors: `SCREEN_FLOOR` (₹300 Cr, ₹1 Cr a day) for Core Setups and the breakout record; `LIQUIDITY_FLOOR` (₹300 Cr, ₹5 Cr a day) for everything that trades. Stocks only the screens list sit in `extraRows` with `liquid: false`; never build breadth, picks or alerts from them.
- Played out lists each stock once per screen (its latest breakout in the last 12 months), like BananaPatterns' "names" count.
- Earlier breakouts (the walk's "rebased" ones) are judged on their own exit rule (`independentExit`): never exited means Climbing or Fresh, exited means Played out. The screen payload is about 6 MB; keep new per-row fields small.
- The stock list holds NSE series EQ and BE (trade-for-trade). BE stocks (`series: "BE"`) are tagged `T2T` on screen rows and are never tradable (`tradable: false` in `computeMetrics`): they appear on the screens and breakout record only. Re-run `npm run update-universe` then `scripts/fetch-market-caps.mjs` weekly.

## Backtest (10-year history)
- `npm`-less scripts: `node --use-system-ca scripts/fetch-history.mjs` downloads 10 years of daily prices to `.cache/history10y/` (resumable; re-run weekly). `scripts/backtest-cli.mjs` / `backtest-compare.mjs` run quick experiments.
- Engine in `src/lib/backtest/` (history, derive, signals, simulate, run). One account, next-open entries, gap-aware stops, costs on both sides, breadth gate, liquidity cap. Tests: `scripts/backtest-sim.test.mjs`.
- `/backtest` page posts settings to `/api/backtest`, which runs `scripts/backtest-job.mjs` in a child process and caches results in `.cache/backtest-results/`.
- Known limits: no historical market cap, survivorship bias (today's stock list).
- 10-year finding: screen breakouts with an 8% stop and 50-day-average trail beat the leaders rule with a fixed 3R target; breadth gate 50–70% all help similarly. The live Top 5 rule and the Buy ready gate are NOT changed yet.

## Live strategy check (/tracker) and the corrected backtest
- `/tracker` follows the rules "Blue sky + Multi-year breakouts" (12% stop by default, 8% as the tighter option, exit under the 50-day average, breadth ≥ 35%, optional Nifty-above-200-day gate that is off by default; see CURRENT RULES) from a start date on real finished daily prices. It replays the backtest engine from the start date to the latest session (`src/lib/backtest/tracker.ts`), so positions, stops, closed trades and "what it would buy at the next open" come from the same code as the 10-year numbers. Paper money only; config in `.cache/strategy-tracker.json`.
- Prices: `scripts/fetch-history.mjs --recent` adds the latest month to every saved file; a scheduler (`historyRefresh.ts`) runs it after 4:30 pm IST on trading days while a tracker exists, and the page has an "Update prices now" button (refused while the market is open: it never saves a forming candle).
- Engine fix (Oct 2026): a buy is now skipped when the cash left covers less than half the size the rules want. Before, ~40% of "trades" were slivers bought with leftover cash, which distorted trade counts, win rate and average R. All numbers quoted in the app were recomputed after this fix: Blue sky ~44%/yr (worst drop 31%); + Multi-year ~46% (27%); with a 12% stop ~47% (21%); Nifty above 200-day ~45% (25%, total losses down about a sixth). "Add to winners" added nothing after the fix and is no longer suggested (the Backtest page still lets you try it).

## AI news check (optional, needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
- `src/lib/market/announcements.ts` reads each stock's last 14 days of NSE announcements (official filings; the summary text only, attachments are not read). `src/lib/ai/newsCheck.ts` makes one Claude call a day (model claude-haiku-5-5, list price $0.10/MTok in, $0.50/MTok out) for the Top picks list and writes one flagged line per stock (clear / watch / caution). The pre-open email shows it; hourly emails reuse the saved notes (`cacheOnly`) and never pay for a call.
- Off by default: with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in `.env.local` nothing is called and the emails are unchanged. Notes and running monthly token totals are in `.cache/news-check.json`. A failure never blocks an email.
- The model sees only the filings it is given, may not predict or advise, and the email says the line can miss or misread a filing.

## Risk gate and plan rehearsal (Oct 2026)
- `src/lib/risk/riskGate.ts`: PASS/WARN/BLOCK for each proposed buy (loss if stopped <= 2% of the account, position <= 20%, <= 10 positions, <= 3 new buys a day, open risk <= 15%, no new buys when the account is down 3% on the day, a stop required, setup check passed, results within 5 days = warning). A block names the reason and the largest passing size. Exits are never blocked. Safety limits, not part of the tested edge. Shown on the trade-plan card (one order vs your capital) and on the Live strategy check (tomorrow's buys, in order, against the real open positions; a holding's working stop is the higher of its stop and its 50-day line).
- `src/lib/backtest/rehearsal.ts` + `PlanRehearsal.tsx` (stock drawer): runs the live rules on one stock's ten-year history with the market gate off and sets its win rate beside the break-even win rate; under 8 trades it says the sample is too small to use. Open question: the drawer's trade plan uses a 2 x ATR stop while Top picks uses the tested 8% stop, so the two can differ.
- Breadth gates, on purpose: the tested breakout setup (Top picks, Live strategy check, banner on Today, trade-plan note, emails' setup lines) uses 35% breadth (the Nifty condition was removed on 31 Oct 2026). The older scanner "Buy ready" lists, Today's Picks, Momentum buy-watch and the 52-week-high breakout section keep `HEALTHY_BREADTH_PERCENT = 50`, because their own backtests (Oct 2024-Sep 2026; 2022-26 weak-watch) lost money below 50%. Do not merge the two without re-running those backtests.

## Strategy health monitor (Oct 2026)
- `src/lib/backtest/health.ts` (+ `healthServer.ts`, `/api/strategy-health`, `StrategyHealthCard` on `/tracker`): compares the rules' last 12 months with every rolling 12-month stretch since 2017, the recent average trade with the earlier one, and (if the live check runs) live average R, win rate, longest losing run (seeded bootstrap) and worst drop with the backtest's. Under 15 live trades or 40 sessions it can only say "early". Owner-only email on the last session of each month. It only warns; it never changes a rule.

## Company health panel (Oct 2026)
- `src/lib/fundamentals/assess.ts` (pure rules + parsers), `fundamentalsServer.ts` (fetch + 12-hour cache), `/api/market/fundamentals?symbol=X[&lender=1]`, `FundamentalsPanel.tsx` in the stock drawer (after the checklist). Five plain checks: sales and profit against the same quarter a year earlier, debt against net worth, promoter holding trend over a year, promoter shares pledged. Verdict: 2+ warnings = weak, 1 = mixed, none and 3+ good = strong.
- Sources: Yahoo `fundamentals-timeseries` (no crumb needed) for quarterly sales/profit and yearly debt/net worth; NSE `corporate-share-holdings-master` and `corporate-pledgedata` for owners and pledges. NSE's financial-results feeds (`results-comparision`, `corporates-financial-results`) stop at Dec 2024 for every stock, so do not use them for growth. Banks/lenders (macro sector "Financial Services") skip the debt check; Yahoo's bank quarterlies are often missing and show "too old to judge".
- Information only. It has no backtest (no point-in-time history), so it never changes Top picks, the setup check, the risk gate or any email. Do not wire it into those without testing it first.
- Top picks cards (`TodayBoard.tsx`) show a small "Company: strong/fine/mixed/weak" tag (`CompanyHealthTag`, nothing while loading or when data is too thin). `src/hooks/useFundamentals.ts` shares one request per stock between the cards and the drawer. The tag is display only: `buildTopPicks` and the order of picks do not read it.

## My positions (Oct 2026)
- Real-money trades the user enters by hand (the app never places orders). `src/lib/positions/positions.ts` (pure: validation, `assessHolding`, journal) + `positionsServer.ts` (file `.cache/positions.json`, written via temp file + rename; `.cache/positions-note.json` remembers the last email) + `/api/positions` (GET view; POST `add | sell | remove`, same-origin only) + `PositionsPage.tsx` at `/positions` (sidebar: Your workspace → My positions).
- Exit rules checked on finished daily candles from `.cache/history10y`: stop hit = a low through the stop on any day after the buy day (the buy day's own low is ignored); exit signal = latest close under the 50-day average (needs 50 candles); near stop = within 3% above it. R uses the original stop and is never recalculated; the stop cannot be edited on purpose.
- Journal needs 10 closed trades before it comments on win rate or average R, and 3+ of both own-call and rule exits before it compares them.
- Emails: after each history refresh, `sendPositionsNoteIfDue` emails the owner only (PERSONAL_ALERT_EMAIL, never EMAIL_TO) when a position has hit its stop or closed under the 50-day average; silent when all is fine; once per day per set of alerts. The history-refresh scheduler now also runs while any open position exists (`hasOpenPositions`), not only while the live strategy check runs.
- Separate from the older "Paper trades & journal" (practice trades, `/api/paper`).

## Strategy tests, 31 Oct 2026 (backtest only; no live rule changed)
- Scripts: `scripts/backtest-recent.mjs` (why the last 12 months were weak; needs `tmp/screen.json` from `/api/market/screen` for sector and market cap), `backtest-variants.mjs` (filters, full period + two halves + last 12 months), `backtest-winrate.mjs` (cost of raising the win rate).
- Last 12 months (+0.05R a trade, 29 trades): concentrated in Jul-Oct 2026 entries (about 15 of 18 stopped out within days in a falling market). RS under 93 and mid-caps lost most, but a minimum-RS filter is not robust across halves (RS 93+ : first half worse, second half better, worst drop -48%).
- Rejected: min RS 90/93, breadth gate 45% (profit 389L -> 118L), ATR stops (helps one half, hurts the other), fixed targets (win rate 46-53% but profit 110L against 389L), faster exits (20/30-day average), break-even stops (win rate falls to 31%).
- Wider 12% stop: win rate 46% (45% in the second half against 37%), profit 412L against 389L, worst drop -21% against -27%; first half profit lower (48L against 56L). The only win-rate lever that did not cost profit. The Live strategy check can run it (stopPercent 12).
- Nifty 50 above 200-day: at an 8% stop about neutral to slightly better (399L against 389L, drawdown -25% against -27%, fewer trades) but with a 12% stop it collapses (146L against 412L). Treat it as fragile: totals depend on a few big winners, so differences of about 10% between variants are noise. Do not present it as a proven improvement.
- Not testable yet: sector-strength filter, market-strength sizing (engine lacks them); size filter (only today's market caps exist).

## 12% stop is the main plan (31 Oct 2026)
- Decision: the main stop is 12% (smaller position, same 2% of the account at risk), not 8%. 10-year test: win rate 46% against 42%, profit 412L against 389L, worst drop -21% against -27%; in the second half 54L against 46L with a 45% against 37% win rate; in the first half profit was lower (48L against 56L). Source: `scripts/backtest-winrate.mjs`.
- Where it lives: `PICK_RULES.stopPercent = 12` in `topPicks.ts` (targets keep the same +16% / +24% price levels: `target1R` 4/3, `target2R` 2); `pickAnalysis.ts` plan has `tighter` (the 8% option) instead of `steadier`; `DEFAULT_STOP_PERCENT = 12` in `positions.ts`; the trade plan card, the checklist stop rule (pass up to 12%, warn up to 16%), the plan rehearsal, the Backtest page default and presets, the Live strategy check form (12% ticked by default) and the Top picks / ready-alert email text. The Live strategy check was restarted on 31 Oct 2026 with the 12% stop and no Nifty filter.
- Not changed on purpose: the older scanner plans (Buy ready, watch list, confluence) and the bottomed-out and 52-week-high sections keep their own stops; `LivePatternSection` breakout-episode texts that say "8% under the breakout close" describe a separate analysis.
- RESOLVED (31 Oct 2026, owner said yes): the setup check no longer requires the Nifty 50 above its 200-day average. `setupStatus` allows real buys on breadth alone (35% of liquid stocks above their 50-day average); the Nifty is still read and shown as information (`niftyOk`, a "not a rule" caution line in the checklist, a note in the pick analysis). Reason: with the 12% stop that filter cut profit from 412L to 146L in the test, and it was only neutral at 8%. Anything above that says the setup needs the Nifty above its 200-day average is out of date.

Keep that sentence next to any quoted backtest figure.

## Watchdog, freshness and the real-browser check (31 Oct 2026)
- `src/lib/positions/watchdog.ts` (started in `instrumentation.ts`, every 2 minutes): while the market is open it emails the owner only (PERSONAL_ALERT_EMAIL, never EMAIL_TO) when a real position's price reaches its stop, and a late-session (from 14:45 IST) heads-up when it trades under its 50-day average; once a day per position and kind (`.cache/positions-live.json`). Pure rules in `liveWatch.ts` (stale prices over 5 minutes, missing or invalid prices never alert). It also raises one freshness alarm a day after 19:30 IST if the saved prices are more than a session old (`.cache/freshness-alarm.json`).
- `src/lib/market/freshness.ts`: `dataFreshness` (a missing candle is only "stale" if the nightly refresh did not run for that day; a refresh that ran means a market holiday, because the holiday calendar only knows fixed national holidays) and `needsCatchUp`. `historyRefresh.ts` now also refreshes outside the after-the-close run when finished sessions are missing and no refresh has run since (once an hour at most), so a laptop that was off through an evening catches up. The Dashboard strip shows a warning line when data is stale.
- The strategy health baseline follows the live check's stop: with the 12% stop the last 12 months read +65% and +0.64R an average trade (verdict on-track); with the 8% stop the same year read +0.05R (verdict watch). Do not quote the old "watch" reading as current.
- Real-browser check (31 Oct 2026): Playwright-core with the installed Chrome and a THROWAWAY profile (never `tmp/bp-profile`), scripts kept outside the repo. Found and fixed: the stock drawer's top banner still said "needs 50%" (it now shows the 35% setup check); the drawer header and stat tiles broke on a 390px screen; `main` containers on /positions, /tracker and /backtest grew wider than the phone because a table with `min-w` sat inside a shrink-to-fit container (fixed with `w-full min-w-0`). Use `scrollWidth > clientWidth` and screenshots at 390px and 1280px after any layout change; `innerText` returns the CSS-uppercased text.
- Reality check (31 Oct 2026): `BacktestSettings.stress` (`slippagePercent`, `gapShare`, `gapLossPercent`, `seed`; engine in `simulate.ts`, validator in `validate.ts`) makes every fill worse and lets a seeded share of stop-outs gap far through the stop. `src/lib/backtest/reality.ts` holds the four scenarios and the plain verdict; `RealityCheck.tsx` (under the year table on `/backtest`) runs them through the normal job API. `scripts/backtest-reality.mjs` result for the live rules (12% stop, no Nifty filter, 10 years, 10 lakh): the test 411L / 46% a year / -21% worst drop; 1% worse fills 189L / 35% / -37%; 15% of stops gapping to -25% about 346L / 43% / -23%; both 153L / 32% / -40%; harsh (1.5% and 30% gapping to -30%) 57L / 21% / -53%. Profitable in every case, but execution quality matters a lot: use limit orders near the open, avoid thin stocks, keep the 2% risk limit.

## Sector limit experiment (31 Oct 2026)
- Engine: `BacktestSettings.maxPerSector` (at most N open positions per sector, best RS first; stocks with no known sector are not limited) using `src/lib/market/data/sectors.json` (759 labels built by `scripts/build-sectors.mjs` from the running app's scan; today's labels are used for past years; about 80% of historical trades have a label). Experiment: `scripts/backtest-sector.mjs`, live rules (12% stop, no Nifty filter).
- Result: 10 years no limit 411L / -21% worst drop; max 4 per sector 420L / -19%; max 3 per sector 430L / -19%; max 2 per sector 409L / -21%; max 1 per sector 360L / -23%. Caps of 3 or 4 were equal or better in both halves (and the last 12 months); a cap of 1 helped the first half and hurt the second. The cap rarely binds (300 trades against 302), so it is a guardrail, not an edge.
- Adopted only as a warning on `/positions` (`SECTOR_LIMIT = 3`, `sectorConcentration` in `positions.ts`, a banner and the sector on each card): nothing is blocked. NOT added to the live strategy check (it would restart the paper test for almost no effect) or to the picks. Rejected: a cap of 1 or 2.
- Not done on purpose: the results-date test (NSE's results feed stops at Dec 2024, it is thousands of calls, the app already warns about results within 14 days).

## Easier interface and a faster way to record trades (31 Oct 2026)
- Sidebar (`Dashboard.tsx`): "Your workspace" now holds Today, My positions, Live strategy check, Backtest (10 years), Watchlist. Everything older is in one collapsed group "Research & older tools" (it includes "Older scanner picks", the former Today's Picks page, and Paper trades & journal). `PageNav.tsx` is a four-link switcher (Today, My positions, Live strategy check, Backtest) at the top of the three standalone pages, replacing their "Back" button.
- The stock drawer no longer shows the old "Status · mid term AVOID" chip beside the price (it contradicted the setup check); its banner is the 35% setup check. The Dashboard strip is three tiles (My positions, Live strategy check, Strategy health): "can I buy" is the banner above it, not repeated.
- "I bought it →" on each buyable Top pick and "Bought it? Add it to My positions" on the trade plan open `/positions?symbol=X&buy=P&stop=S`. The form is pre-filled (the stop is rounded DOWN to a 5-paise tick), the price paid defaults to the planned buy price and can be corrected, and the suggested shares come from `suggestedShares` (2% of the account at risk, one position at most 20%) worked out from the PLANNED price so correcting the price paid never changes the share count. Account size is the shared `useAccountSize` hook (`sa.accountSize.v1`): the position-size calculator, the trade plan card and the My positions form all use it. `src/hooks/useAccountSize.ts` is the ORIGINAL hook (returns `{ accountSize, setAccountSize }`): an earlier slip overwrote it with a different version; it was restored exactly from the dev build's source map. Check for an existing file before creating a hook.
- `Holding.plannedPrice` (optional) records the plan; cards show "Planned ₹X · paid +y% above the plan", `fillSummary` gives the average over positions with a plan and the page compares it with the reality check's 1% worse fills; the CSV has "Planned price" and "Paid vs plan (%)" columns.
- The trade plan card's risk check now receives the real open positions from `/api/positions` (it used an empty list before), so the position-count and open-risk limits can fire.
- Number boxes for prices must use `step="any"`: `step="0.05"` made the browser silently refuse prices like 362.41 or a pick's stop of 317.02.
- Not done on purpose: a phone bottom tab bar and tabs inside the stock drawer (the sidebar rail works on phones; both are bigger layout changes with little gain), and the glossary/first-run guide.

## Tomorrow's plan email and the UI check (31 Oct 2026)
- Tomorrow's plan (owner-only, OPT-IN): `src/lib/positions/tomorrowPlan.ts` (pure: `buildTomorrowPlan`, `planEmail`; tests `scripts/tomorrow-plan.test.mjs`), `planServer.ts` (`sendTomorrowPlanIfDue`, called after each successful evening history refresh from `instrumentation.ts`), `account.ts` + `/api/account` (GET, POST, DELETE; file `.cache/account.json`). The email is sent to PERSONAL_ALERT_EMAIL only (never EMAIL_TO), only when ALL hold: the user turned it on (saving the account size is the opt-in; the "Plan email on/off" switch on My positions), the saved prices are fresh, the market check passed (breadth >= 35%) and at least one breakout fits. Silent otherwise; once per set of orders (`.cache/tomorrow-plan.json`).
- It uses `BacktestResult.pending.candidates` (new, optional): every breakout-day signal on the last close that the market gates allow, best RS first, with no paper-account limits (RESULT_VERSION is now 5 so old saved results refresh). The planner then applies the REAL account: positions already held, at most 3 per sector, results within 5 days = wait, 2% at risk with a 20% size cap (`suggestedShares`), the risk gate's limits (10 positions, 15% open risk, 3 new buys a day; a buy is cut to the most that passes or skipped with the reason), and a 5% "skip if it opens above" limit. Orders are for the next open; the stop is 12% under the signal close. The app still never places orders.
- Replay check with real data (31 Oct 2026, no email sent): on past days when breadth passed, the planner produced 2 to 3 orders of about 1.65 lakh each on a 10 lakh account, with the other candidates listed as skipped.
- `npm run check:ui` (`scripts/check-ui.mjs`, devDependency `playwright-core`): opens the main pages and the stock drawer at 1280 and 390 px in Chrome with a throwaway profile and reports sideways scrolling, script errors, failed requests and missing key text, with screenshots in `tmp/ui-check`. `-- --flow` also runs the "I bought it" flow with a throwaway position that it removes again. Fyers 401s are ignored (the charts fall back to Yahoo). Run it after any layout change, with the site up.

## Email track record (`/radar`)
Every stock a real pre-open or hourly email lists is saved the first time it appears, then scored against the finished daily prices, so we can see whether the stocks we send out actually work. Nothing in it sends mail or changes a rule.
- **Recording:** `recordEmailedStocks()` in `src/lib/radar/radarServer.ts`, called right after a successful `sendEmail` in `sendPreOpenEmailNow` and `sendHourlyEmailNow` only (test emails never record). It never throws. Lists recorded: Top picks (tag ready/broke/watch/extended), Weekly Top 5 (only when the pre-open email showed it, i.e. no Top picks), older Buy ready list, older watch list, scanner agreement and bottomed-out (hourly only). The preview objects expose `emailed` (pre-open) and `emailedPicks` (hourly) for this.
- **File:** `.cache/email-picks.json` (atomic write, a daily copy in `.cache/backups/email-picks-DATE.json`, newest 30 kept). One entry per stock + list + tag; a stock listed again within 10 days only bumps `lastDay`/`mentions`; a tag change (Watch to Ready) or a return after more than 10 days is a new entry.
- **Scoring (`src/lib/radar/radar.ts`, pure):** the email price is the buy price; stop = the email's own, else 12% under. Stopped out when a day's low reaches the stop (gap = at the open); exit signal when the close is under the 50-day average (only once the stock has been above it, so bottomed-out and scanner ideas are not "exited" on day one); stop assumed first if stop and target share a day. A pre-open email counts its own session, an hourly email starts the next one. Also plain 5- and 20-session moves (ignoring the stop), best/worst, first-target hit, R, and the move minus the Nifty 50. Groups under 30 scored stocks are labelled "too few to judge".
- **Page:** `/radar` (`RadarPage.tsx`, `GET /api/radar`), in the sidebar under Your workspace and in `PageNav`. Tests: `scripts/radar.test.mjs`. Not built yet: back-filling past emails (their lists cannot be rebuilt reliably).

## Phone bottom tab bar
`MobileTabBar` (in `src/app/layout.tsx`) shows five tabs at the bottom of a phone screen (under 640px) on `/`, `/positions`, `/tracker`, `/backtest` and `/radar` only: Today, Positions, Live check, Backtest, Emails. Styles are `.tabbar*` in `globals.css` (navy bar, gold current tab; the body and the sidebar rail leave room for it via `--tabbar-h`). On a phone the `PageNav` pill row is hidden because the bar replaces it. "Today" while already on the Dashboard resets the hash view itself (pushState + popstate) because the Dashboard reads its view from the address hash. `npm run check:ui` checks the bar is present on phones only and marks the right tab. New weekly pages should be added to `TABS` here and in `PageNav`.

## Glossary (tap-to-explain words)
`src/lib/glossary.ts` holds 15 plain-language meanings (R, stop, 50-day exit, market check, RS, breakout, Blue sky, Multi-year breakout, position size, win rate, worst drop, backtest, versus Nifty, paper trade, target). Its numbers (12% stop, 35% market check, 2%/20% sizing, about 45% win, about 21% worst drop) must be updated there whenever a rule changes; `scripts/glossary.test.mjs` checks them. `<Term k="r">` (`src/components/Term.tsx`) draws a dotted-underline word that opens a note on tap/click/keyboard (fixed to the screen so it never widens the page; closes on outside tap, scroll or Escape). It is used on Backtest, My positions, Live check and Email track record; `GlossaryList` shows every word on About & risk. `Stat` labels may now be nodes. New jargon should get an entry and a `<Term>`.
